sentences.zh: 凯撒、哈里发、沙皇，他们曾征服过广袤的世界。

sentences.en: They proclaimed themselves the favorites of the gods, and yet their empires crumbled away.
sentences.zh: 他们自诩为神的宠儿，然而他们的帝国终究分崩离析。

sentences.en: As my lady Elizabeth is put from that degree she was in, and what degree she is at now, I know not by hearsay.
sentences.zh: 至于我的夫人伊丽莎白被降了身份，以及她现在的地位如何，我并非道听途说。

sentences.en: I know not how to order her or myself or her women or grooMs.
sentences.zh: 我不知道该如何安排她、我自己、她的随从女官还是马夫。

sentences.en: I beg you to be good lord to her and hers, and that she may have raiment, for she has neither gown, nor kirtle, nor petticoot, nor linen for smocks, nor kerchiefs, sleeves, rails,
sentences.zh: 恳请您对她和她的人多加关照，并让她能有衣物可穿，因为她既没有长裙、Kirtle裙、衬裙，也没有做内衣的亚麻布、头巾、衣袖、饰带、

sentences.en: bodices, handkerchiefs, mufflers, nor caps.
sentences.zh: 胸衣、手帕、围巾，也没有帽子。

sentences.en: So, we'll discover who that was in a couple of moments.
sentences.zh: 那么，我们过一会儿就会揭晓刚才那是谁。

sentences.en: Was it Mrs. Thatcher?
sentences.zh: 是撒切尔夫人吗？

sentences.en: No, it definitely was not.
sentences.zh: 不，绝对不是。

sentences.en: But these are very, very dark days for the infant Elizabeth I, as she will become.
sentences.zh: 但对于日后将成为伊丽莎白一世的这位幼小公主来说，这些是非常非常黑暗的日子。

sentences.en: She's not yet three years old, but she doesn't have enough mufflers.
sentences.zh: 她还不到三岁，却连围巾都不够用。

sentences.en: There's no kerchiefs, there's no kirtle, there's no gown, there's no bodice.
sentences.zh: 没有头巾，没有Kirtle裙，没有长裙，也没有胸衣。

sentences.en: And there's no mummy.
sentences.zh: 而且没有妈妈。

sentences.en: There's no mummy.
sentences.zh: 没有妈妈。

sentences.en: I mean, this is a terrible, terrible scene.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个非常非常糟糕的场景。

sentences.en: So, if you listened to our previous episode, well, if you didn't listen to our previous episode, what are you doing?
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你听了我们上一期节目——好吧，如果你没听我们上一期节目，你在干什么呢？

sentences.en: But if you listened to our previous episode and recall it, you will know that Elizabeth's father, Henry VIII, has severed the head of her mother, Anne Boleyn,
sentences.zh: 但如果你听了上一期节目并且还记得的话，你就会知道伊丽莎白的老爹亨利八世砍掉了她母亲安妮·博林的头，

sentences.en: because he's fed up with her being a bit of a nag, and also fed up with her not giving him a son.
sentences.zh: 因为他受够了她爱唠叨，也受够了她没能为自己生个儿子。

sentences.en: And he is very keen to marry his new lady friend, the excitingly boring Jane Seymour.
sentences.zh: 而且他非常急着想娶他的新女伴——那个无趣却又令人兴奋的简·西摩。

sentences.en: So, Anne is out, mummy is dead, and we ended last time by saying, what will this mean for Elizabeth I, and how will she fare in the snake pit of Henry's court?
sentences.zh: 所以，安妮出局了，妈妈死了，我们在上一期结尾时说过，这对伊丽莎白一世意味着什么，她在亨利那危机四伏的宫廷里又会过得怎么样？

sentences.en: And now we will find out.
sentences.zh: 现在我们就来揭晓答案。

sentences.en: And the first bit of bad news, no handkerchiefs.
sentences.zh: 而第一个坏消息是：没有手帕。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, Tom, let's put people out of their misery.
sentences.zh: 那么，汤姆，我们来为听众解开谜团吧。

sentences.en: That was not Margaret Thatcher, that was Lady Bryan.
sentences.zh: 那不是玛格丽特·撒切尔，那是布莱恩夫人。

sentences.en: Yeah, which is a great name, I think.
sentences.zh: 对，我觉得这也是个很棒的名字。

sentences.en: And Lady Bryan is the sort of Mary Poppins.
sentences.zh: 而且布莱恩夫人有点像是玛丽·波平斯。

sentences.en: Yeah, so she's in her 60s.
sentences.zh: 对，她当时已经六十多岁了。

sentences.en: She's actually Elizabeth's great aunt.
sentences.zh: 她其实是伊丽莎白的大姨妈。

sentences.en: And so she was the obvious choice to serve Elizabeth as her lady mistress, as it was known, which is, as you said, a kind of very posh Mary Poppins.
sentences.zh: 所以她是担任伊丽莎白女总管（当时是这么称呼的）的不二人选，正如你所说，这就像是一个非常高档的玛丽·波平斯。

sentences.en: And Lady Bryan is facing up to the fact that Elizabeth, who previously had been so fated, had been so privileged, now suddenly all that privilege seems to have gone.
sentences.zh: 布莱恩夫人不得不面对这样一个现实：伊丽莎白以前备受宠爱、享尽特权，而现在突然之间，所有这些特权似乎都消失了。

sentences.en: And poor Elizabeth, you know, not yet four, is kind of immersed in, effectively, a very dark fairy tale.
sentences.zh: 可怜的伊丽莎白，你知道的，不到四岁就 praticamente 陷入了一个非常黑暗的童话故事中。

sentences.en: So she's no longer the heir to the throne.
sentences.zh: 因此她不再是王位继承人。

sentences.en: She's now officially proclaimed a bastard.
sentences.zh: 她现在被官方宣布为私生子。

sentences.en: She's no longer a princess.
sentences.zh: 她不再是公主了。

sentences.en: She's just the Lady Elizabeth.
sentences.zh: 她只是伊丽莎白小姐。

sentences.en: Henry VIII has ordered that she be kept from his sight.
sentences.zh: 亨利八世下令不准让她出现在自己的视线范围内。

sentences.en: So she had been at Greenwich Palace when her mother was executed.
sentences.zh: 所以她母亲被处决时，她正在格林尼治宫。

sentences.en: She's been sent away.
sentences.zh: 她被送走了。

sentences.en: Henry doesn't want her there.
sentences.zh: 亨利不想让她待在那儿。

sentences.en: And Henry's also ordered that her household be cut back.
sentences.zh: 而且亨利还下令削减她的随从规模。

sentences.en: And then on top of that, there's this further cruelty.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，还有更进一步的残忍对待。

sentences.en: So to quote David Starkey in his book Apprenticeship, the shower of lovely clothes which Anne Boleyn had lavished on her daughter suddenly dried up.
sentences.zh: 用大卫·斯塔基在他的书《学徒期》中的话来说，安妮·博林曾倾注在女儿身上的那些漂亮衣服突然就断了供给。

sentences.en: And in fact, as Starkey points out, this wasn't conscious cruelty on Henry's part, but it was still neglect.
sentences.zh: 事实上，正如斯塔基所指出的，这并不是亨利有意为之的残酷，但依然是一种忽视。

sentences.en: It's still expressive of the fact that he's not really bothered about Elizabeth anymore.
sentences.zh: 这依然表明了他其实根本不在乎伊丽莎白了。

sentences.en: And definitely, Henry has his mind on other things than worrying about his baby daughter.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，亨利的心思全在别的事情上，根本没空去操心他那幼儿期的女儿。

sentences.en: Jane Seymour specifically, right?
sentences.zh: 具体来说就是简·西摩，对吧？

sentences.en: Because just 10, 11 days after Anne Boleyn has been executed, he gets married to Jane Seymour.
sentences.zh: 因为就在安妮·博林被处决后的第10天、第11天，他就和简·西摩结婚了。

sentences.en: He does.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And he sails with her down the Thames to Greenwich, which is, of course, the palace where Anne had been arrested.
sentences.zh: 他带着她乘船顺着泰晤士河来到格林尼治，当然，那正是安妮被捕的宫殿。

sentences.en: And Jane, who had been the lady-in-waiting to Anne, now presides in Greenwich as Queen.
sentences.zh: 而曾是安妮女侍官的简，如今作为王后在格林尼治主政。

sentences.en: Henry also has another issue on his mind, which is what to do with his elder daughter, Mary,
sentences.zh: 亨利心头还有另一个问题，那就是如何处理他的大女儿玛丽，

sentences.en: who has been a permanent source of annoyance to him ever since he got rid of Mary's mother, Catherine of Arrogate.
sentences.zh: 自从他抛弃了玛丽的母亲阿拉贡的凯瑟琳之后，玛丽就一直是他源源不断的烦恼来源。

sentences.en: Mary by now is 20.
sentences.zh: 玛丽当时已经20岁了。

sentences.en: She remains devoted to the memory of her mother, who'd been unceremoniously dumped by Henry for Anne Boleyn.
sentences.zh: 她依然深切缅怀她的母亲，那位被亨利为了安妮·博林而极不体面地抛弃的母亲。

sentences.en: She is devoted to not just the memory of her mother, who's dead by now, but also to the faith of her mother, traditional Catholic faith.
sentences.zh: 她不仅深念着如今已经过世的母亲的记忆，也坚守着她母亲的信仰——传统的罗马天主教信仰。

sentences.en: And so she's absolutely obdurate in her refusal to accept that Henry might be the head of the Church of England rather than the Pope.
sentences.zh: 因此，她极其顽固地拒绝承认亨利是英国教会的领袖而非教皇。

sentences.en: And this has been the sticking point between Henry and Mary ever since Henry's supremacy over the Church of England was announced.
sentences.zh: 自从亨利宣布自己为英国教会最高领袖以来，这就一直是亨利和玛丽之间不可调和的矛盾焦点。

sentences.en: But now, in the wake of Anne Boleyn's death, she does kind of briefly waver.
sentences.zh: 但在安妮·博林死后，她确实有过短暂的动摇。

sentences.en: And I think in part because Jane, unlike Anne, shows Mary great favour.
sentences.zh: 我想部分原因是因为简与安妮不同，对玛丽非常恩宠。

sentences.en: She's very kind to her.
sentences.zh: 对她很好。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, we said Jane was boring.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们说过简很无趣。

sentences.en: Jane is a very nice person, isn't she?
sentences.zh: 简是个非常好的人，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think so.
sentences.zh: 对，我也这么觉得。

sentences.en: I applaud Jane for this.
sentences.zh: 我为简这一点点赞。

sentences.en: And I think also Mary must be missing her father.
sentences.zh: 而且我想玛丽一定也很想念父亲。

sentences.en: I mean, she hasn't seen him for years.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，她已经好几年没见过他了。

sentences.en: You know, he's basically banished her because she's been so annoying.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他基本上把她放逐了，因为她太让人烦心了。

sentences.en: And so Henry senses his opportunity to finally get Mary to submit.
sentences.zh: 所以亨利察觉到了最终让玛丽屈服的机会。

sentences.en: And so he sends down a party of peers and they ride down to see Mary in Hertfordshire.
sentences.zh: 于是他派了一行贵族前往赫特福德郡探望玛丽。

sentences.en: And they convince her to yield.
sentences.zh: 他们说服了她妥协。

sentences.en: And they tell her if she was their daughter, they would beat her and knock her head so violently against the wall that they would make it as soft as baked apples.
sentences.zh: 他们告诉她，如果她是他们的女儿，他们就会狠狠揍她，把她的头往墙上猛撞，直到把她的头撞得像烤苹果一样软。

sentences.en: It's harsh.
sentences.zh: 这话说得很重。

sentences.en: And it has to be said, you know, there's quite a lot of violence being threatened against Mary.
sentences.zh: 必须承认，你知道的，玛丽受到了相当多的暴力威胁。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, imagine that if you're a 20 year old girl and all these blokes and gilets turn up and start saying they're going to splash your head against the wall.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，想象一下，如果你是一个20岁的女孩，这一帮穿背心的糙汉突然出现，开始说要把你的脑袋往墙上砸。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Anyway, finally, she submits.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，最终她妥协了。

sentences.en: She signs the articles that acknowledge Henry as head of the English church.
sentences.zh: 她签署了承认亨利为英国教会最高领袖的条款。

sentences.en: And of course, this is a surrender that also requires her to acknowledge that her mother's marriage to her father had been incestuous and unlawful.
sentences.zh: 当然，这次屈服也要求她承认她母亲与父亲的婚姻是乱伦且非法的。

sentences.en: And it's really the one moment in her life when she buckles, when she doesn't stick to her principles.
sentences.zh: 这确实是她一生中唯一一次妥协，唯一一次没有坚持原则。

sentences.en: So Nicola Tallis in her book on young Elizabeth writes, she would never forgive herself for what she believed to be the ultimate portrayal of her mother's memory.
sentences.zh: 因此，尼古拉·塔利斯在她关于年轻伊丽莎白的书中写道：她永远不会原谅自己做出了她认为是对母亲记忆的终极背叛。

sentences.en: And I think in the long run, actually, it serves just to make her even more determined to uphold her principles.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为从长远来看，这实际上只会让她更加坚定地坚守自己的原则。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Now, in the last episode, I revealed myself as, although not an admirer of Mary's ideological position, a great admirer of Mary as a person.
sentences.zh: 现在，在上一集里，我表明了虽然我并不欣赏玛丽的意识形态立场，但我非常欣赏玛丽这个人。

sentences.en: And actually, she now behaves very nicely to Elizabeth, doesn't she?
sentences.zh: 而且实际上，她现在对伊丽莎白非常好，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because she and Elizabeth are now equal because Elizabeth has been declared a bastard as well.
sentences.zh: 因为她和伊丽莎白现在扯平了，由于伊丽莎白也被宣布为私生子。

sentences.en: And Mary turns out to be a very nice sister, older sister for Elizabeth.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，玛丽是伊丽莎白一个非常好的姐姐、年长的姐姐。

sentences.en: So people always think of them as daggers drawn, but that's not entirely the case.
sentences.zh: 所以人们总是认为她们水火不容，但事实并非完全如此。

sentences.en: So she says, from this point on, I shall never call her by other name than sister.
sentences.zh: 因此她说：从今以后，我绝不称呼她为别的名字，只会叫她妹妹。

sentences.en: No longer is she that little bastard.
sentences.zh: 她不再是那个小私生子了。

sentences.en: She's now her sister.
sentences.zh: 她现在是她的妹妹了。

sentences.en: And as you say, she's very loving.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，她非常慈爱。

sentences.en: She gives Elizabeth all kinds of toys, plays with her, all kinds of things like that.
sentences.zh: 她送给伊丽莎白各种各样的玩具，陪她玩，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And she even amazingly brings herself to pray for the soul of Anne Boleyn.
sentences.zh: 甚至让人惊叹的是，她竟然说服自己为安妮·博林的灵魂祈祷。

sentences.en: That's pretty magnanimous, given how Anne Boleyn had treated her.
sentences.zh: 考虑到安妮·博林曾如何对待她，这可以说是相当宽宏大量了。

sentences.en: That really is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So again, to quote David Starkey on Mary, he says that she was tenderhearted to excess when issues of principle were not involved.
sentences.zh: 所以再次引用大卫·斯塔基对玛丽的评价，他说当不涉及原则问题时，她有着过度的菩萨心肠。

sentences.en: Like me.
sentences.zh: 就像我一样。

sentences.en: I thought that you were flinty hearted even when issues of principle weren't involved.
sentences.zh: 我还以为你即使在不涉及原则问题时也铁石心肠呢。

sentences.en: No, I think actually I'm a very sentimental person.
sentences.zh: 不，我觉得其实我是一个非常感性的人。

sentences.en: Do you?
sentences.zh: 是吗？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Go on, continue.
sentences.zh: 行吧，你继续。

sentences.en: So Elizabeth.
sentences.zh: 那么伊丽莎白。

sentences.en: So what about her?
sentences.zh: 那她怎么样？

sentences.en: She's a very precocious little girl, but also I think profoundly unsettled and must be in a state of some bewilderment because she is aware of her change in circumstances.
sentences.zh: 她是一个非常早熟的小女孩，但也同样深感不安，一定处于某种迷茫状态，因为她意识到了自己处境的巨变。

sentences.en: So there's this comment she makes to the man who's essentially responsible for her security.
sentences.zh: 所以她对那个基本上负责她安全的人说过这样一番话。

sentences.en: And she says, why, Governor, how happy yesterday, Lady Princess and today but Lady Elizabeth.
sentences.zh: 她说：天呐，总督大人，昨天还是快乐的公主殿下，今天却只成了伊丽莎白小姐。

sentences.en: And so at some point, obviously, she is told about what has happened to her mother.
sentences.zh: 所以在某个时刻，很显然，有人把发生在她母亲身上的事告诉了她。

sentences.en: We don't know when.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道具体是何时。

sentences.en: And as far as we can tell from our extant sources, she never really mentions Anne's name.
sentences.zh: 据我们从现存资料中能了解到的，她从未真正提及过安妮的名字。

sentences.en: And I think it's clear why she doesn't, because her claim to the throne is massively not helped by the fact that her mother had her head chopped off for treason.
sentences.zh: 我想原因很明显，因为她的母亲因为叛国罪被砍了头，这对于她宣称王位继承权是毫无帮助的。

sentences.en: She clearly does hold Anne's memory in her heart because as queen, she will surround herself with any number of Berlin relatives.
sentences.zh: 她心里显然一直铭记着安妮，因为日后当上女王后，她身边聚拢了数不清的博林家族亲戚。

sentences.en: And she owns this locket ring made of mother of pearl and studied with diamonds and rubies.
sentences.zh: 她拥有一个由珍珠母制成、镶嵌着钻石和红宝石的挂坠戒。

sentences.en: And when she opened it, it revealed paired miniature portraits.
sentences.zh: 当她打开它时，里面是一对微型肖像画。

sentences.en: So one of herself and one of Anne.
sentences.zh: 一个是她自己，另一个是安妮。

sentences.en: So clearly, the memory of Anne does matter to her.
sentences.zh: 所以很显然，安妮的记忆对她而言很重要。

sentences.en: But the fact she doesn't talk about it perhaps may be expressive of a kind of buried trauma as well as of kind of political sense.
sentences.zh: 但她绝口不谈此事，或许也表达了一种深埋心底的创伤，以及某种政治上的敏锐感。

sentences.en: How much would she genuinely remember of Anne, though?
sentences.zh: 不过，她对安妮到底能真正记住多少呢？

sentences.en: I don't think she would remember anything.
sentences.zh: 我想她什么也不会记得。

sentences.en: But I think the notion that her mother had been executed by her father must be a kind of deep psychic wound.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得母亲被父亲处决这件事，一定在她心灵深处留下了深深的创伤。

sentences.en: I can't believe it would have been anything other than that.
sentences.zh: 我深信绝不会是别的什么。

sentences.en: Fair enough.
sentences.zh: 也罢。

sentences.en: People who are interested in exploring the nuances of it.
sentences.zh: 对于有兴趣深入了解其中细微之处的人，

sentences.en: Tracy Borman's book, Anne Boleyn and Elizabeth, is really, really good on the whole subject.
sentences.zh: 特蕾西·博尔曼写的书《安妮·博林与伊丽莎白》把这个话题写得非常非常好。

sentences.en: Let's get to the really important issue, which is the lack of handkerchiefs.
sentences.zh: 我们来谈谈真正重要的问题，那就是缺乏手帕。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Lady Bryan.
sentences.zh: 布莱恩夫人。

sentences.en: Lady Bryan has complained.
sentences.zh: 布莱恩夫人抱怨了。

sentences.en: No girdle, no bodice.
sentences.zh: 没有腰带，没有胸衣。

sentences.en: That's crucial lack.
sentences.zh: 这是致命的物资匮乏。

sentences.en: Is that ever addressed?
sentences.zh: 这曾经得到解决吗？

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So Elizabeth's clothing allowance is upgraded.
sentences.zh: 所以伊丽莎白的服装津贴提高了。

sentences.en: She gets her kerchiefs and kirtles and all that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 她得到了头巾、裙子和诸如此类的东西。

sentences.en: But I think that despite that, there's no question that she is now growing up conscious of being second best to her elder sister, Mary.
sentences.zh: 但我认为尽管如此，毫无疑问，她现在长大时已经意识到自己不如她的姐姐玛丽。

sentences.en: Because Jane Seymour, you know, really fusses over Mary, does her best to make her feel happy, but pretty much ignores Elizabeth.
sentences.zh: 因为你知道，简·西摩确实对玛丽百般呵护，尽最大努力让她感到快乐，但基本上忽视了伊丽莎白。

sentences.en: And again, you can see why.
sentences.zh: 同样，你可以理解为什么。

sentences.en: I mean, just as Mary had been a reminder to Anne Boleyn of Henry's first wife.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，正如玛丽曾让安妮·博林想起亨利的结发妻子一样。

sentences.en: So Elizabeth is a reminder to Jane Seymour of his second wife.
sentences.zh: 因此，伊丽莎白让简·西摩想起他的第二任妻子。

sentences.en: So you can understand the psychology of it.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以理解其中的心理。

sentences.en: And then on the 12th of October, 1547, Elizabeth becomes third best because that is when Jane gives Henry a son.
sentences.zh: 然后在1547年10月12日，伊丽莎白降到了第三位，因为那是简给亨利生下一个儿子的日子。

sentences.en: And although Jane dies two weeks later, this son, Edward, survives.
sentences.zh: 尽管简在两周后去世了，但这个名叫爱德华的儿子活了下来。

sentences.en: And this means at last, Henry has his male heir.
sentences.zh: 这意味着亨利终于有了他的男性继承人。

sentences.en: And it also means for Elizabeth that she loses the services of Lady Brian, which is very sad because she is now assigned as lady mistress to the young prince.
sentences.zh: 这也意味着伊丽莎白失去了布赖恩夫人的照顾，这非常令人难过，因为她现在被指派为年轻王子的女总管。

sentences.en: She's the best lady mistress in the business.
sentences.zh: 她是这一行里最优秀的女总管。

sentences.en: And so obviously the young prince must have her.
sentences.zh: 显而易见，年轻的王子必须由她来照料。

sentences.en: But I think, again, this must have been a blow to Elizabeth because really Lady Brian had kind of filled the maternal void left by Anne's execution.
sentences.zh: 但我想，这对于伊丽莎白来说一定是个打击，因为布赖恩夫人确实填补了安妮被处决后留下的母爱空白。

sentences.en: And Elizabeth, by this point, I mean, she's only just four.
sentences.zh: 而此时的伊丽莎白，我的意思是，她才刚满四岁。

sentences.en: You know, she's lost her mother, who she presumably barely remembers, and now she's lost her mother's substitute.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，她失去了母亲——她可能对母亲没什么记忆，现在她又失去了母亲的替代者。

sentences.en: And again, I don't think it's over-psychologizing to see that this must have had an impact on Elizabeth.
sentences.zh: 同样，我认为过度心理分析并不为过，可以看出这必定对伊丽莎白产生了影响。

sentences.en: Because from this point on, she always forms very, very intense relationships with her personal attendants.
sentences.zh: 因为从这一点开始，她总是与她的贴身侍从建立非常非常强烈的情感关系。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And hugs them very close to her.
sentences.zh: 并且与她们极其亲近。

sentences.en: And once she's decided that an attendant is loyal to her, she will basically never let her go.
sentences.zh: 一旦她认定某个侍从对她忠心耿耿，她基本上就绝不会放她离开。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Even great characters in history, human beings first and foremoSt.
sentences.zh: 即使是历史上的伟人，首先也是普通人。

sentences.en: And a child who's had a very disruptive and traumatic beginning to their life is bound to want to find maternal figures to whom they can cling for affection.
sentences.zh: 一个在生活中经历过颠沛流离和创伤的儿童，注定会想要寻找可以依恋以获取关爱的母亲形象。

sentences.en: And that's the case, isn't it, with the very first of these.
sentences.zh: 首当其冲的正是这种情况，对吧？

sentences.en: So Lady Brian has gone and there's a series of governesses.
sentences.zh: 所以布赖恩夫人离开了，接着来了一系列家庭女教师。

sentences.en: The first one has the splendid sort of American style name of Catherine Champanown.
sentences.zh: 第一个女教师有着极具美式风格的美丽名字——凯瑟琳·钱帕诺恩。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: I mean, what name is that?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是什么名字？

sentences.en: Kate.
sentences.zh: 凯特。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Kate Champanown.
sentences.zh: 凯特·钱帕诺恩。

sentences.en: She will stick with Elizabeth up to her death decades in the future.
sentences.zh: 她将陪伴伊丽莎白直到几十年后她去世。

sentences.en: So people who've watched Blackadder.
sentences.zh: 所以看过《黑爵士》的人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: To the degree that anyone is Nursey in Blackadder.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，就像《黑爵士》里的南西。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Kate is.
sentences.zh: 凯特就是这样。

sentences.en: So Queen Elizabeth in Blackadder is very spoiled.
sentences.zh: 所以《黑爵士》里的伊丽莎白女王非常被宠坏。

sentences.en: You know, school girl.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，像个女学生。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And Nursey is kind of absolute dimwit.
sentences.zh: 而南西有点像个十足的笨蛋。

sentences.en: Tis brought the twinkling of a toe since you could say nothing but Lizzie go plop plop.
sentences.zh: 自从你只会说莉兹去扑通扑通以来，她就带来了脚趾的一闪而过。

sentences.en: Lizzie go plop plop.
sentences.zh: 莉兹去扑通扑通。

sentences.en: So she's a kind of idiot in Blackadder.
sentences.zh: 所以在《黑爵士》里她是个某种程度上的白痴。

sentences.en: It has to be said that Kate Champanown is absolutely not an idiot.
sentences.zh: 必须说明的是，凯特·钱帕诺恩绝对不是个白痴。

sentences.en: She's an amazing woman.
sentences.zh: 她是一个了不起的女性。

sentences.en: She's a great scholar.
sentences.zh: 她是一位伟大的学者。

sentences.en: She's a humaniSt.
sentences.zh: 她是一位人文主义者。

sentences.en: She's an evangelical.
sentences.zh: 她是一位福音派信徒。

sentences.en: And she's probably the person who in her life, I would guess, Elizabeth loves more than anyone else.
sentences.zh: 我猜她可能是伊丽莎白一生中最爱的人，超过了其他人。

sentences.en: And Elizabeth says of Kate, she has taken great labor and pain in bringing of me up in learning and honesty.
sentences.zh: 伊丽莎白这样评价凯特：她在培养我学习和诚实方面付出了巨大的劳苦和心血。

sentences.en: So, you know, that's a fine tribute.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这是一个极高的赞誉。

sentences.en: But I think credit is also due to Elizabeth herself because it is already becoming apparent, you know, when she's still quite young, that she's really very, very smart.
sentences.zh: 但我认为伊丽莎白本人也功不可没，因为当她还很年轻的时候，就已经很明显她非常非常聪明。

sentences.en: And there were specialists in education who worried that Kate was actually pushing Elizabeth too far.
sentences.zh: 当时有一些教育专家担心凯特实际上把伊丽莎白逼得太紧了。

sentences.en: And one of these people was a man who wasn't just England's foremost Greek scholar, but was also the greatest educationalist in the country.
sentences.zh: 其中一人不仅是英格兰最顶尖的希腊语学者，也是国内最伟大的教育家。

sentences.en: And this is a guy called Roger Asham, who, again, like Kate, is an evangelical.
sentences.zh: 这个人叫罗傑·阿沙姆，他跟凯特一样，也是个福音派信徒。

sentences.en: So there's a kind of sense that humanist scholarship, evangelical beliefs, devotion to education, it's part of the swirl that Elizabeth is in.
sentences.zh: 所以有一种感觉，人文主义学识、福音派信仰、对教育的奉献，都是伊丽莎白所处环境的一部分。

sentences.en: But Asham thinks, oh, you know, we mustn't hurry this.
sentences.zh: 但阿沙姆认为，哦，你知道，我们不能操之过急。

sentences.en: We mustn't push it too far.
sentences.zh: 我们不能把她逼得太紧。

sentences.en: But actually, on this occasion, he's wrong because Elizabeth really flourishes under Kate's educational regime to the degree that in December 1539, one of Henry's courtiers comes
sentences.zh: 但事实上，这一次他错了，因为伊丽莎白在凯特的教育体制下真正蓬勃发展，以至于在1539年12月，亨利的一位朝臣来到

sentences.en: to Hatfield, where Elizabeth is based, to pay a courtesy call.
sentences.zh: 伊丽莎白所在的哈特菲尔德进行礼节性拜访。

sentences.en: She's six years old at this time.
sentences.zh: 她当时六岁。

sentences.en: He talks to her and he's completely stunned by what he finds.
sentences.zh: 他与她交谈，被她的表现彻底惊呆了。

sentences.en: And he reports back to Henry, if she be no more educated than she now appeareth to be, she will prove of no less honor and womanhood than she'll be seen her father's daughter.
sentences.zh: 他向亨利汇报说，如果她受到的教育不比现在所表现出来的更多，她将展现出不亚于其父之女的荣誉和女性风范。

sentences.en: So in other words, you know, she's a massive chip off the old block.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，你知道，她完全继承了乃父之风。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And actually, this courtier says she's as smart as a woman of 40 years old.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这位朝臣说她和一个四十岁的女人一样聪明。

sentences.en: So very, very impressive.
sentences.zh: 所以非常非常令人印象深刻。

sentences.en: And from this point on, you know, Henry is sufficiently intrigued that he wants regular updates on Elizabeth's progress.
sentences.zh: 从这个时候起，你知道，亨利产生了足够的兴趣，他希望定期了解伊丽莎白进展的最新情况。

sentences.en: And this isn't just her progress as a scholar, but also her abilities as a musician, which matters to Henry a lot.
sentences.zh: 这不仅是她作为学者的进展，还包括她作为音乐家的才华，这对亨利来说非常重要。

sentences.en: You know, can she dance?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，她会跳舞吗？

sentences.en: Can she sew?
sentences.zh: 她会缝纫吗？

sentences.en: Is she good at riding?
sentences.zh: 她擅长骑马吗？

sentences.en: Can she hawk?
sentences.zh: 她会玩鹰猎吗？

sentences.en: And actually, she's good at all these things.
sentences.zh: 事实上，她样样精通。

sentences.en: I mean, this is one thing about the Tudors that perhaps, because they're ubiquitous and because they're always the subjects of kind of Channel 5 documentaries and stuff, therefore
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，关于都铎王朝有一点，也许是因为他们无处不在，而且总是成为第五频道纪录片之类的主题，因此

sentences.en: people are a little bit sick of them.
sentences.zh: 人们有点厌烦他们了。

sentences.en: Sort of man for man, woman for woman.
sentences.zh: 就个人而言。

sentences.en: They are extremely impressive.
sentences.zh: 他们极其令人印象深刻。

sentences.en: They are surely the most proficient and impressive dynasty in English history.
sentences.zh: 他们无疑是英国历史上最精干、最令人瞩目的王朝。

sentences.en: I mean, the reason they've got the throne as usurpers, as parvenues, is because they are very canny, bright, talented, ambitious, driven people.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们作为篡位者、暴发户登上王位的原因，是因为他们是非常精明、聪慧、有才华、有雄心、有进取心的人。

sentences.en: You know, the Tudors don't produce a wastrel.
sentences.zh: 你知道，都铎家族没有出一个败家子。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And they just seem to be good at everything.
sentences.zh: 而且他们似乎做什么都擅长。

sentences.en: Elizabeth sounds an absolute prodigy, but clearly people are amazingly impressed by her.
sentences.zh: 伊丽莎白听起来简直是个神童，但显然人们对她印象深刻极了。

sentences.en: And Henry is sufficiently impressed that by 1543, he's decided, okay, I'm going to rehabilitate her.
sentences.zh: 亨利印象深刻，到1543年时他决定，好吧，我要恢复她的地位。

sentences.en: You know, I like the sound of her.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我挺中意她的。

sentences.en: She sounds like she might be a credit to me.
sentences.zh: 她听起来可能会为我增光添彩。

sentences.en: And this is a really key moment in Elizabeth's life because, you know, for as long as she can remember, Henry has been this distant, terrifying figure.
sentences.zh: 这是伊丽莎白生命中一个真正关键的时刻，因为，你知道的，在她有记忆以来，亨利一直是个遥远而可怕的人物。

sentences.en: The man who had executed her mother, she hadn't seen him.
sentences.zh: 那个处决了她母亲的男人，她一直没见到他。

sentences.en: She's been literally banished from his presence.
sentences.zh: 她字面意义上被逐出了他的视线。

sentences.en: And of course, she's also aware that it's due to her father's ruling that she's inferior in rank to Mary as well as to Edward.
sentences.zh: 当然，她也很清楚，正是由于她父亲的裁决，她在地位上才落后于玛丽以及爱德华。

sentences.en: And I think also something else that must be slightly destabilizing to Elizabeth emotionally,
sentences.zh: 我想还有另一件事一定让伊丽莎白在情感上感到有些不安，

sentences.en: but also complicate her attitude to Henry, is the fact that he just keeps burning through stepmothers.
sentences.zh: 同时也使她对亨利态度复杂，那就是他不停地更换继母。

sentences.en: So Jane dies.
sentences.zh: 所以简去世了。

sentences.en: Then he marries Anna Cleaves, decides he doesn't want her.
sentences.zh: 然后他娶了克里夫的安妮，又决定不想要她。

sentences.en: Then he marries Catherine Howard, and Catherine Howard ends up having her head chopped off on charges of adultery, just as Anne had done.
sentences.zh: 接着他娶了凯瑟琳·霍华德，而凯瑟琳·霍华德最终因通奸罪被砍了头，正如安妮的下场一样。

sentences.en: So I think that must be very traumatic for Elizabeth.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这对于伊丽莎白来说一定非常具有创伤性。

sentences.en: But fortunately for her, once Henry allows her back into his life, she does impress him.
sentences.zh: 但幸运的是，一旦亨利允许她重回他的生活，她确实给他留下了深刻的印象。

sentences.en: He does think this girl is really quite something.
sentences.zh: 他确实觉得这个女孩相当了不起。

sentences.en: And I think partly that's because she's very smart, but it's also because she really looks like him.
sentences.zh: 我想部分原因是因为她非常聪明，但也是因为她长得真的很像他。

sentences.en: You know, she's got auburn hair.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，她有一头红褐色的头发。

sentences.en: She's got fair skin.
sentences.zh: 她有着白皙的皮肤。

sentences.en: I mean, fortunately, she's not enormously fat, which would have been awful, but she looks like a Tudor.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，幸运的是她没有胖得离谱，那可就太糟糕了，但她看起来像个都铎家人。

sentences.en: You know, she is her father's daughter.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，她就是她父亲的女儿。

sentences.en: She's very clearly been welcomed back into the fold, as has Mary.
sentences.zh: 很显然，她和玛丽一样被重新接纳回了家族核心。

sentences.en: So when he marries Catherine Parr, so that's wedding number six, all three of the children are there, Edward, Mary and Elizabeth.
sentences.zh: 所以当他娶凯瑟琳·帕尔时——那是第六次婚礼，三个孩子都在场：爱德华、玛丽和伊丽莎白。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And she's still a bastard, right?
sentences.zh: 而她仍然是个私生女，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, Henry has not, will never withdraw that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，亨利没有，也永远不会撤销这一点。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So this act of parliament establishes that Edward will succeed him.
sentences.zh: 所以这项国会法案确立了爱德华将继承他的王位。

sentences.en: If Edward has no children, then Mary will become queen.
sentences.zh: 如果爱德华没有孩子，那么玛丽将成为女王。

sentences.en: And if Mary then dies without children, then Elizabeth will become queen.
sentences.zh: 如果玛丽去世时也没有孩子，那么伊丽莎白将成为女王。

sentences.en: But with kind of absolute typical inconsistency, Henry does not repeal the acts of bastardy.
sentences.zh: 但带有绝对典型的出尔反尔，亨利并没有废除私生子法案。

sentences.en: So this is going to be an issue for both Mary and Elizabeth throughout their reigns, essentially.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，这将成为玛丽和伊丽莎白在其整个统治期间一直要面对的问题。

sentences.en: But I think at the time, the fact that Elizabeth has been reinstated in the line of succession, she sees it as a mark of Henry's love for her.
sentences.zh: 但我认为当时伊丽莎白重返继承序列这一事实，被她视为亨利爱她的标志。

sentences.en: And people may wonder, well, what is Elizabeth's attitude to Henry, this guy who had killed her mother?
sentences.zh: 人们可能会想，伊丽莎白对亨利——这个杀死她母亲的男人——究竟是什么态度？

sentences.en: So David Starkey puts it, her memory of her father formed in these few years of the mid
sentences.zh: 正如大卫·斯塔基所言，她对父亲的记忆，在1540年代中期这短短几年里形成的是良性的。

sentences.en: 1540s was a benign one.
For Elizabeth, he was not a wife murdering monster, but a loving parent, a formidable ruler and model to which she aspired.
sentences.zh: 对伊丽莎白来说，他不是一个谋杀妻子的怪物，而是一个慈爱的父亲、一个令人生畏的统治者以及她所崇拜的榜样。

sentences.en: And I think that's largely true, but I think it must also obviously be seasoned with a certain sense of dread.
sentences.zh: 我认为这很大程度上是真实的，但也必须夹杂着某种程度的恐惧。

sentences.en: But you can dread someone and still want their approval.
sentences.zh: 但你可以畏惧某个人，却依然渴望得到他们的认可。

sentences.en: Totally.
sentences.zh: 完全如此。

sentences.en: Crave their approval.
sentences.zh: 渴望他们的认可。

sentences.en: I mean, even when he's in his sort of fat phase, he's still a very magnetic and charismatic personality.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，即使在他那种发福的阶段，他仍然是一个极具吸引力和个人魅力的存在。

sentences.en: And a little girl, we're talking about when she's eight, nine, ten or something.
sentences.zh: 而一个小女孩，我们说的是她八岁、九岁、十岁左右的时候。

sentences.en: You know, he's the king.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他是国王。

sentences.en: He's the son around whom everybody else revolves.
sentences.zh: 他是每个人都围绕着旋转的太阳。

sentences.en: Of course, she'd be drawn to him and impressed and she'd be, if nothing else, awed by his magnificence and by the fear that he inspires in other people.
sentences.zh: 当然，她会被他吸引，留下深刻印象，并且除此以外，她也会被他的宏大以及他在其他人心中激起的恐惧所折服。

sentences.en: So Henry's definitely an influence, but I think a much bigger influence on Elizabeth is her new stepmother, Catherine Parr.
sentences.zh: 所以亨利绝对是一个影响，但我认为对伊丽莎白影响更大的是她的新继母凯瑟琳·帕尔。

sentences.en: So the new queen who, a bit like Anne Boleyn or Jane Seymour, not from a tremendously distinguished background.
sentences.zh: 新王后有点像安妮·博林或简·西摩，并非来自显赫的背景。

sentences.en: She's the daughter of a knight from Cumbria, but she's clever.
sentences.zh: 她是坎布里亚郡一名骑士的女儿，但她很聪明。

sentences.en: She's very cultured, very sexy, even though she's in her early thirties, with apologies to women who are in their early thirties.
sentences.zh: 她很有文化，非常迷人，尽管她已经三十出头了——向三十出头的女性致歉。

sentences.en: Even though, Tom, even though.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，汤姆，尽管如此。

sentences.en: I am repeating the standards of the age.
sentences.zh: 我只是在重复那个时代的标准。

sentences.en: Early thirties was quite old by Tudor standards.
sentences.zh: 按都铎时期的标准，三十出头已经相当老了。

sentences.en: She's also an evangelical, so that's a slight issue because by this point, Henry is kind of reverting to pretty much a Catholic identity, but that's fine.
sentences.zh: 她也是个福音派信徒，所以这有点问题，因为到这个时候，亨利基本上正在回归天主教的身份，但这没关系。

sentences.en: Catherine keeps that secret.
sentences.zh: 凯瑟琳把这保守得很好。

sentences.en: But there's another thing that she also keeps secret, which is that she is in love with another man.
sentences.zh: 但她还保守着另一个秘密，那就是她爱上了另一个男人。

sentences.en: And this other man is the brother of Henry's late wife, Jane Seymour, Thomas Seymour.
sentences.zh: 这个男人是亨利已故妻子简·西摩的兄弟托马斯·西摩。

sentences.en: And obviously, Catherine Parr does not need to be told that this is a very dangerous thing for any queen to be involved with.
sentences.zh: 显而易见，凯瑟琳·帕尔不需要别人提醒就知道，任何王后卷入这种事都是非常危险的。

sentences.en: And all the more so because Thomas Seymour is very charismatic, very good looking.
sentences.zh: 更何况托马斯·西摩极具魅力、长相英俊。

sentences.en: So he's described as being fierce in courage, courtly in fashion, in personage, stately.
sentences.zh: 因此他被形容为勇气勇猛、举止宫廷化、风度翩翩。

sentences.en: He has an astonishingly long beard.
sentences.zh: 他留着一把惊人长的大胡子。

sentences.en: And of course, also, he is not morbidly obese and he doesn't have a weeping sore on his leg, both of which attributes Henry by this point does have.
sentences.zh: 当然，他也既没有病态肥胖，腿上也没有流脓的溃疡，而亨利在这个时候这两样都有。

sentences.en: But still, there's no way that Catherine is going to carry on with Thomas Seymour.
sentences.zh: 但尽管如此，凯瑟琳绝对不可能继续和托马斯·西摩在一起。

sentences.en: So she encourages him to go off to war in France, where he fights very bravely with Henry in a campaign that culminates in the capture of Boulogne.
sentences.zh: 因此，她鼓励他去法国参战，在那里他与亨利并肩英勇作战，这场战役以攻占布洛涅告终。

sentences.en: And meanwhile, back in England, Catherine is ruling as regent, which she does very well, rather as Catherine of Aragon had done all those decades before.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，在英国本土，凯瑟琳以摄政身份执政，她做得非常好，就像几十年前的阿拉贡的凯瑟琳一样。

sentences.en: And again, this must be quite a formative influence, I think, on both Mary and Elizabeth, because it's a demonstration that women can govern the kingdom effectively and well.
sentences.zh: 而且同样，我认为这对玛丽和伊丽莎白来说都具有相当大的塑造作用，因为这证明了女性能够有效且出色地治理王国。

sentences.en: And that must serve as a kind of inspiration for them, I think, later in life.
sentences.zh: 我认为，这必定会成为她们日后生活的一种鼓舞。

sentences.en: And Elizabeth particularly ends up devoted to Catherine, who takes her duties as stepmother very seriously.
sentences.zh: 伊丽莎白尤其对凯瑟琳深表爱戴，凯瑟琳非常认真地履行着继母的职责。

sentences.en: Catherine is an impressive person.
sentences.zh: 凯瑟琳是一个令人印象深刻的人。

sentences.en: She's smart and she's, you know, poised, but she's also canny.
sentences.zh: 她很聪明，你知道的，举止优雅，而且她也很精明。

sentences.en: I mean, the whole thing with Thomas Seymour, she doesn't make the mistake that Catherine
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，关于托马斯·西摩这件事，她没有犯下凯瑟琳

sentences.en: Howard made, for example.
sentences.zh: 霍华德那样犯下的错误，比如说。

sentences.en: She's also very stylish.
sentences.zh: 她也非常时髦。

sentences.en: I mean, like Anne Boleyn, she loves her fashion.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，就像安妮·博林一样，她热爱时尚。

sentences.en: And just as Anne Boleyn had done, she understands that a queen has to look like a queen.
sentences.zh: 就像安妮·博林过去那样，她明白女王必须看起来像个女王。

sentences.en: And so I think all in all, she becomes a huge influence on Elizabeth, who she keeps fixing her attentions on would-be stepmothers and they keep vanishing.
sentences.zh: 所以总的来说，我认为她对伊丽莎白产生了巨大的影响，伊丽莎白总是把注意力放在那些准继母身上，而她们却不断消失。

sentences.en: And now she feels, well, at last I've got one that, you know, that's a keeper.
sentences.zh: 现在她觉得，好吧，我终于找到了一个，你知道的，能留得住的人。

sentences.en: And this matters because Catherine becomes stepmother at a crucial point in Elizabeth's intellectual development.
sentences.zh: 这很重要，因为凯瑟琳在伊丽莎白智力发展的关键时期成为了她的继母。

sentences.en: And you said Catherine Parr is a very kind of smart woman.
sentences.zh: 你刚才说凯瑟琳·帕尔是一个非常聪明的女性。

sentences.en: She takes a great interest in Elizabeth's education, because by this point, Elizabeth has outgrown Kate's ability to teach her.
sentences.zh: 她对伊丽莎白的教育表现出极大兴趣，因为此时的伊丽莎白已经超出了凯特教导她的能力范围。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, this doesn't matter because Elizabeth, by this point, is growing up alongside her younger brother, Edward.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，这并没有关系，因为此时的伊丽莎白正和她年幼的弟弟爱德华一同长大。

sentences.en: And because Edward is going to become a king, inevitably, he has the best teachers in the country at his service.
sentences.zh: 由于爱德华注定要成为国王，他不可避免地拥有全国最好的老师来为他服务。

sentences.en: And so Catherine convinces Henry that Elizabeth should have use of these teachers as well.
sentences.zh: 因此，凯瑟琳说服亨利，让伊丽莎白也能接受这些老师的教导。

sentences.en: Edward is smart.
sentences.zh: 爱德华很聪明。

sentences.en: He's a Tudor, but Elizabeth is much smarter.
sentences.zh: 他是都铎王朝的人，但伊丽莎白聪明得多。

sentences.en: Everyone recognises that.
sentences.zh: 所有人都承认这一点。

sentences.en: And so by the time she's 10, she's the focus of this kind of really brilliant circle.
sentences.zh: 因此，在她十岁的时候，她就成为了这个真正才华横溢的圈子的核心。

sentences.en: It's characterised by humanist scholarship and by evangelical religion.
sentences.zh: 它的特点是人文主义学者风气和福音派宗教信仰。

sentences.en: So kind of what we might start to call Protestantism.
sentences.zh: 也就是我们开始称之为新教的东西。

sentences.en: And the key figure is a guy called William Grindle, who is a young scholar from St. John's,
sentences.zh: 核心人物是一个叫威廉·格林德尔的人，他是圣约翰学院的一名年轻学者，

sentences.en: Cambridge, and he teaches both Latin and Greek.
sentences.zh: 来自剑桥，他同时教拉丁语和希腊语。

sentences.en: And the emphasis on Greek is very, very of the moment.
sentences.zh: 对希腊语的重视在当时非常非常合时宜。

sentences.en: So Henry only had the most rudimentary Greek.
sentences.zh: 所以亨利只懂最基础的希腊语。

sentences.en: Mary had no Greek.
sentences.zh: 玛丽不懂希腊语。

sentences.en: Elizabeth is getting the kind of the latest in educational fashion.
sentences.zh: 而伊丽莎白正在接受最新潮的教育。

sentences.en: And Elizabeth develops a profound emotional as well as intellectual bond with Grindle.
sentences.zh: 伊丽莎白对格林德尔产生了深厚的情感以及理智上的羁绊。

sentences.en: And I think it intensifies her sense of loyalty to Catherine as well, because it's Catherine who seems to have found her, Grindle, to be her teacher.
sentences.zh: 我认为这也加深了她对凯瑟琳的忠诚感，因为似乎正是凯瑟琳发掘了格林德尔来做她的老师。

sentences.en: There's further kind of emotional churn, because listeners to our previous episode may remember that Anne Boleyn had as her private chaplain a man called Matthew Parker.
sentences.zh: 这里还有一层情感上的波澜，因为收听我们上一集的听众可能记得，安妮·博林曾有一位名叫马修·帕克的私人牧师。

sentences.en: And in her last interview with him before she got taken to the Tower, she had asked Matthew
sentences.zh: 在她被带往伦敦塔之前的最后一次谈话中，她曾请求马修

sentences.en: Parker to look out for Elizabeth.
sentences.zh: 帕克关照伊丽莎白。

sentences.en: And this is what Matthew Parker is now doing.
sentences.zh: 这就是马修·帕克现在正在做的事。

sentences.en: He's coming and giving sermons to Elizabeth and instructing her and all kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 他前来向伊丽莎白讲道、指导她以及做各种各样的事情。

sentences.en: So that is, I think, intensifying what must for Elizabeth be a very emotional as well as intellectual sense of loyalties, that it is tied up with her mother.
sentences.zh: 所以我想，这正在强化对伊丽莎白而言既有极深的情感、又有理智色彩的忠诚感，这种忠诚与她的母亲紧密相连。

sentences.en: It's tied up with Catherine Parr, her stepmother.
sentences.zh: 它也与她的继母凯瑟琳·帕尔紧密相连。

sentences.en: There's kind of love as well as religion and education as part of the swirl.
sentences.zh: 在这种风云变幻中，既有爱，也有宗教和教育。

sentences.en: So you don't think there's any doubt whatsoever that Elizabeth grows up a strong believer in the newly fashionable, let's just call it Protestantism.
sentences.zh: 所以你认为毫无疑问，伊丽莎白长大后坚信那种新近风靡的宗教——我们暂且叫它新教吧。

sentences.en: I think so.
sentences.zh: 我也这么认为。

sentences.en: And I think the big influence on her is Catherine Parr.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为对她影响最大的是凯瑟琳·帕尔。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 真有趣。

sentences.en: And Catherine Parr, she's from a generation where a kind of hard Protestant identity hasn't yet evolved, but that's clearly the direction of travel.
sentences.zh: 而凯瑟琳·帕尔，她属于这样一代人：坚定严苛的新教身份尚未真正形成，但那显然是发展的方向。

sentences.en: And I think you can see how this is affecting Elizabeth emotionally from two New Year gifts that she makes.
sentences.zh: 我想你可以从她制作的两份新年礼物中看出这对伊丽莎白在情感上的影响。

sentences.en: First, she makes and gives to Catherine Parr in 1545.
sentences.zh: 首先，她在1545年制作并送给了凯瑟琳·帕尔一份礼物。

sentences.en: And then the second, the following year, is to Henry himself.
sentences.zh: 然后第二年，她送给了亨利本人第二份礼物。

sentences.en: So the first, the one that she gives to the Queen, this is a translation from French of a poem by Marguerite of Navarre.
sentences.zh: 第一件，也就是她送给王后那件，是一首由纳瓦拉的玛格丽特所写诗歌的法语译本。

sentences.en: And people may remember that Marguerite of Navarre had been the patron of Anne Boleyn, Elizabeth's mother.
sentences.zh: 人们可能还记得，纳瓦拉的玛格丽特曾是伊丽莎白母亲安妮·博林的赞助人。

sentences.en: And it's very evangelical in tone.
sentences.zh: 它的基调非常具有福音派色彩。

sentences.en: So again, that mingling of emotional loyalty with kind of proto-Protestantism, it's all there.
sentences.zh: 所以再次说明，情感忠诚与原始新教倾向的交织，全都体现在那里了。

sentences.en: And then the second gift, the one that Elizabeth presents to Henry, this is a translation of
sentences.zh: 然后是第二件礼物，伊丽莎白献给亨利的那件，这是对

sentences.en: Catherine's own prayers and meditations, which she'd written in English.
sentences.zh: 凯瑟琳自己的祈祷文和沉思录的翻译，那些是她用英语写的。

sentences.en: And Elizabeth has translated into French, into Italian, and into Latin.
sentences.zh: 而伊丽莎白将其翻译成了法语、意大利语和拉丁语。

sentences.en: And at the point where she does this, she is 12 years old.
sentences.zh: 在她做这件事的时候，她只有12岁。

sentences.en: So, you know, it's her first year at secondary school.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，这是她上中学的头一年。

sentences.en: I mean, it's unbelievably impressive.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这令人难以置信地印象深刻。

sentences.en: How standards have fallen, Tom.
sentences.zh: 现在的标准下降了多少啊，汤姆。

sentences.en: Yeah, how standards have fallen.
sentences.zh: 是啊，标准下降了多少。

sentences.en: And what's more, she's embroidered the cover.
sentences.zh: 而且更厉害的是，她还绣了封面。

sentences.en: So she's kind of, she's made the binding as well and embroidered it with Tudor roses.
sentences.zh: 所以她甚至自己做好了装订，并用都铎玫瑰将其绣好。

sentences.en: And she dedicates it to the most illustrious and most mighty King Henry VIII, Elizabeth, his majesty's most humble daughter, wishes all happiness and begs his blessing.
sentences.zh: 她把它献给最显赫、最强大的国王亨利八世，陛下最卑微的女儿伊丽莎白祝愿他一切幸福并祈求他的祝福。

sentences.en: And this is tribute, not just to her father, but to her stepmother as well.
sentences.zh: 这不仅是对她父亲的致敬，也是对她继母的致敬。

sentences.en: And so when Henry dies, which he does on the 28th of January, 1547, so that's a year after Elizabeth had made that gift.
sentences.zh: 因此，当亨利去世时——他在1547年1月28日去世，也就是伊丽莎白送出那份礼物的整整一年后。

sentences.en: And he succeeded by Edward VI, who by this point is nine years old, so still just a boy.
sentences.zh: 继位的是爱德华六世，此时他九岁，所以依然只是个男孩。

sentences.en: To be fair to him, he's very bright in his own right.
sentences.zh: 平心而论，他本身非常聪明。

sentences.en: Yeah, he's very bright as well.
sentences.zh: 是的，他也非常聪明。

sentences.en: But I think he's not as brilliant as Elizabeth is.
sentences.zh: 但我认为他没有伊丽莎白那么才华横溢。

sentences.en: And so Elizabeth, she now turns to Catherine Parr to basically provide her with a home.
sentences.zh: 因此，伊丽莎白现在转向凯瑟琳·帕尔，基本上是为了给自己找个栖身之所。

sentences.en: And so a few weeks after Henry's died, Elizabeth moves to Chelsea, where the widowed queen has moved into one of the queen's manor houses.
sentences.zh: 所以在亨利去世几周后，伊丽莎白搬到了切尔西，这位寡居女王已经搬进了其中一处王后宅邸。

sentences.en: It's a very lovely spot.
sentences.zh: 那是个非常可爱的风水宝地。

sentences.en: It's got pipe water.
sentences.zh: 那里有自来水。

sentences.en: It's got cherry and peach trees, herb gardens, lots of, you know, hay nonny knowing, all that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 那里有樱桃树和桃树、草药园，还有许多，你知道的，寻欢作乐、各种各样的好玩事物。

sentences.en: And with Elizabeth goes her beloved lady mistress, Kate, who is now, she's just got married.
sentences.zh: 与伊丽莎白一同前往的有她深爱的主管女官凯特，她现在刚结过婚。

sentences.en: So she's now known as Kate Ashley or Astley.
sentences.zh: 所以她现在被称为凯特·阿什利或阿斯特利。

sentences.en: Elizabeth also has in her train her new cofferer, her kind of business manager, the guy who looks after her accounts.
sentences.zh: 伊丽莎白随从队伍中还有她的新财务总管，也就是她的业务经理、负责打理她账目的人。

sentences.en: And this is a man called Thomas Parry.
sentences.zh: 这个人名叫托马斯·帕里。

sentences.en: And we have lots of Welsh listeners who complain that we don't have enough Welsh figures, Welsh characters in our podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 我们有很多威尔士听众抱怨说，我们的播客里没有足够的威尔士人物、威尔士角色。

sentences.en: So I will read you the description that Starkey gives of Thomas Parry, that he was a fat, self-satisfied
sentences.zh: 所以我来读一下斯塔基对托马斯·帕里的描述，说他是一个肥胖、自我感觉良好的

sentences.en: Welshman.
sentences.zh: 威尔士人。

sentences.en: That's great.
sentences.zh: 这太棒了。

sentences.en: So it's very clear what David Starkey thinks of Welshman from that quote.
sentences.zh: 所以从那段引文可以非常清楚地看出大卫·斯塔基对威尔士人的看法。

sentences.en: And also, he's not very good at maths.
sentences.zh: 而且，他的数学不太好。

sentences.en: So that doesn't make him a very competent cofferer.
sentences.zh: 所以这让他当不成一个称职的财务总管。

sentences.en: So he's useless.
sentences.zh: 所以他是个废物。

sentences.en: He's fat.
sentences.zh: 他又胖。

sentences.en: He's useless.
sentences.zh: 他又没用。

sentences.en: He's fat, but he is Welsh.
sentences.zh: 他又胖又没用，但他是个威尔士人。

sentences.en: So there's one positive.
sentences.zh: 所以这也是个优点。

sentences.en: Oh, and also another positive from Elizabeth's point of view.
sentences.zh: 哦，从伊丽莎白的角度来看，还有另一个优点。

sentences.en: You know, he's a Protestant and he's exceptionally loyal to her.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他是新教徒，而且对她极为忠诚。

sentences.en: You know, we like to do Welsh history every now and again, don't we?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们总喜欢时不时地讲讲威尔士历史，对吧？

sentences.en: And we've done it now.
sentences.zh: 而我们现在已经讲过了。

sentences.en: So that's brilliant.
sentences.zh: 所以这太棒了。

sentences.en: We've done it for the year.
sentences.zh: 我们今年份的已经做完了。

sentences.en: And Thomas himself has become the Lord High Admiral because, of course, both of them are the uncles of the young king, Edward VI.

sentences.en: So, for Thomas Seymour to marry a late queen, it's a punchy thing to do because, you know, he's massively punching above his weight there.
sentences.zh: 所以，托马斯·西摩迎娶一位已故女王是一件极具冲击力的事，因为，你知道的，他这完全是癞蛤蟆想吃天鹅肉。

sentences.en: And so, when the news breaks, there is outrage at court.

sentences.en: And the consequences of this, you called Thomas Seymour Mr. Tickle.
sentences.zh: 而这带来的后果，你把托马斯·西摩称为蒂克尔先生。

sentences.en: Well, let's say that the consequence of this is that the tickle hands can start tickling.
