sentences.en: Hello, welcome back to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到《历史的沉淀》。

sentences.en: So, we are in England in 1548.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们来到了1548年的英格兰。

sentences.en: We are a year in to the reign of the ultra-Protestant, very precocious, Edward VI.
sentences.zh: 当时正值极端新教徒、非常早熟的爱德华六世登基满一年。

sentences.en: And specifically, we are in Seymour Place, which is the home of Edward's uncle, Thomas Seymour, who you may remember, has married Edward's stepmother, Catherine Parr,
sentences.zh: 具体来说，我们在西摩宅邸，这里是爱德华的叔叔托马斯·西摩的住所，大家可能还记得，他娶了爱德华的继母凯瑟琳·帕尔，

sentences.en: the widow of Henry VIII.
sentences.zh: 也就是亨利八世的遗孀。

sentences.en: And Catherine Parr is pregnant, and here we are, all sweetness and light, because her stepdaughter, the teenage Lady Elizabeth, 14 years old, has just arrived at the house,
sentences.zh: 凯瑟琳·帕尔当时正在孕期，瞧我们现在这副一团和气、其乐融融的样子，因为她的继女、十多岁的伊丽莎白女士，也就是14岁，刚刚来到这座宅邸，

sentences.en: having been away for the festive season.
sentences.zh: 此前她一直在外度过节日季。

sentences.en: So, there's another girl there, actually, who we've had on The Rest is History before, who's another very clever girl, another girl with aristocratic lineage,
sentences.zh: 所以，其实这里还有另一个女孩，我们在《历史的沉淀》里以前也介绍过，她也是个非常聪明的女孩，同样有着贵族血统，

sentences.en: another girl who loves a bit of Latin and a bit of Greek, and loves Protestantism.
sentences.zh: 同样是个热爱拉丁语、希腊语并信仰新教的女孩。

sentences.en: And this is somebody called Lady Jane Grey, who's only 11 years old.
sentences.zh: 她就是简·格雷女士，当时只有11岁。

sentences.en: She's 11 years old, and she's Thomas Seymour's ward, and she's Elizabeth's cousin.
sentences.zh: 她只有11岁，是托马斯·西摩的受监护人，也是伊丽莎白的表妹。

sentences.en: And, as you said, Dominic, we did a couple of episodes on Lady Jane Grey, and people who want to listen to those episodes, they are 293 and 294.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，多米尼克，我们曾做过几期关于简·格雷女士的节目，想要收听这些节目的听众，可以去找第293期和第294期。

sentences.en: Now, Dominic, you said that all is sweetness and light at Seymour Place in London.
sentences.zh: 那么，多米尼克，你刚才说伦敦的西摩宅邸里一片其乐融融。

sentences.en: I'm not actually sure that's quite true.
sentences.zh: 我其实觉得这话未必完全属实。

sentences.en: It's just a figure of speech, Tom.
sentences.zh: 这只是一种修辞，汤姆。

sentences.en: I'm just setting the scene.
sentences.zh: 我只是在交代背景。

sentences.en: Sometimes there's tears behind the smiles.
sentences.zh: 有时笑容背后也藏着眼泪。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, you know, at Christmas, there are always a dark undertow.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道的，在圣诞节期间，总会有一些黑暗的暗流。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So, for starters, Elizabeth is yet again in a state of bereavement, because William Grindle, her beloved teacher, had died a few weeks before.
sentences.zh: 首先，伊丽莎白正处于又一次失去亲人的悲痛之中，因为她深爱的老师威廉·格林德尔在几周前去世了。

sentences.en: It's not all bad, because just a few days before arriving at Seymour Place, she'd received a letter from Grindle's own teacher, the great educationalist Roger Asham,
sentences.zh: 不过也不算太糟，因为就在抵达西摩宅邸的前几天，她收到了格林德尔自己的老师、伟大的教育家罗杰·阿沙姆的一封信，

sentences.en: offering to take Grindle's place.
sentences.zh: 信中提议由他来取代格林德尔的位置。

sentences.en: And Elizabeth completely leaps at the chance.
sentences.zh: 伊丽莎白对这个机会毫不犹豫地抓住了。

sentences.en: I mean, it's an amazing opportunity for her, because Asham is the most famous, the most brilliant scholar in England.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这对她来说是个绝佳的机会，因为阿沙姆是英格兰最著名、最才华横溢的学者。

sentences.en: And Asham promises that he will finesse Elizabeth's education, but also that he will look out for her.
sentences.zh: 阿沙姆承诺他将进一步雕琢伊丽莎白的学业，同时也会照顾好她。

sentences.en: So he writes, I shall think it my greatest happiness if the time ever comes when my services can be of use to you.
sentences.zh: 于是他写道，如果有一天我的服务能对您有所用处，我将视其为我最大的幸福。

sentences.en: And I think these words would have had great resonance for Elizabeth, because actually, her circumstances in Seymour Place,
sentences.zh: 我想这些话对伊丽莎白来说一定有着深远的共鸣，因为事实上，她在西摩宅邸的处境，

sentences.en: no matter how devoted she is to Catherine Parr, her stepmother, are actually not easy at all.
sentences.zh: 无论她多么深爱她的继母凯瑟琳·帕尔，其实一点也不轻松。

sentences.en: So firstly, you mentioned Catherine's pregnant.
sentences.zh: 所以首先，你提到了凯瑟琳怀孕了。

sentences.en: It's the first time she's been pregnant.
sentences.zh: 这是她第一次怀孕。

sentences.en: I think this is probably a bit destabilising for an orphaned girl who, you know, up to this point had been the sole focus of her stepmother's attentions.
sentences.zh: 我想这对于一个孤女来说可能有点让人心神不宁，毕竟在此之前，她一直是继母关注的唯一焦点。

sentences.en: And perhaps worries about being supplanted yet again.
sentences.zh: 也许她会担心自己再次被取代。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think so.
sentences.zh: 是的，我也这么觉得。

sentences.en: But that, Dominic, is not the main reason why there is an atmosphere in Seymour Place.
sentences.zh: 但多米尼克，那并不是西摩宅邸气氛微妙的主要原因。

sentences.en: The main reason is because of the long-bearded, ludicrously ambitious, top lad, Thomas Seymour.
sentences.zh: 主要原因在于那个留着长胡子、荒谬地野心勃勃的顶级大帅哥，托马斯·西摩。

sentences.en: So Thomas Seymour is the younger brother of the Duke of Somerset, who's the Lord Protector.
sentences.zh: 所以托马斯·西摩是萨默塞特公爵的弟弟，而萨默塞特公爵是护国公。

sentences.en: And he's resentful of this.
sentences.zh: 他对这一点心怀怨恨。

sentences.en: You know, it's kind of classic, kind of Prince Harry dynamic.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这有点像哈里王子那种经典的动态关系。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You know, resentful of the elder brother, wants him out the way.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，对兄长心怀怨恨，想把他弄走。

sentences.en: He's kind of on manoeuvres, plotting to try and supplant his elder brother.
sentences.zh: 他一直在四处活动，密谋试图取代他的兄长。

sentences.en: So maybe there's a kind of slight degree of mood of anxiety in Seymour Place for that reason.
sentences.zh: 所以也许正因为如此，西摩宅邸里多少带有一点焦虑的情绪。

sentences.en: But there's a much more immediate personal reason for Elizabeth to be uncomfortable in Thomas Seymour's presence.
sentences.zh: 但对于伊丽莎白来说，在托马斯·西摩面前感到不自在，还有一个更直接、更私人的原因。

sentences.en: And that is basically that for the past few months, Thomas Seymour has had the key to Elizabeth's bedroom.
sentences.zh: 那就是基本上在过去的几个月里，托马斯·西摩一直拿着伊丽莎白卧室的钥匙。

sentences.en: And basically every morning he's got into the habit of walking into her bedroom.
sentences.zh: 而且基本上每天早晨他都养成了走进她卧室的习惯。

sentences.en: And it's reported later that if Elizabeth was up and in the process of getting dressed, he would come up and strike her upon the back or on the buttocks.
sentences.zh: 据后来报道，如果伊丽莎白已经起床并正在穿衣，他就会走过来拍打她的背部或臀部。

sentences.en: If she was still in bed, he'd pull back the curtains, you know, that veil her, the four poster beds, as though he would come at her and Elizabeth would shrink back,
sentences.zh: 如果她还在床上，他就会拉开那些帷幔，你知道的，就是将她遮住的四柱床的幔帐，仿佛他要朝她扑过去，而伊丽莎白则会往后缩，

sentences.en: cower beneath the sheets.
sentences.zh: 瑟缩在被子下面。

sentences.en: On one occasion, it's reported he tries to force a kiss.
sentences.zh: 据报道，有一次他试图强吻她。

sentences.en: Kate goes and confronts him about this and he shows no kind of embarrassment about this, but instead explodes in rage.
sentences.zh: 凯特去质问了他这件事，而他对此毫无尴尬之意，反而勃然大怒。

sentences.en: I will tell my Lord Protector how I am slanded and I will not leave off for I mean no evil.
sentences.zh: 我要去告诉护国公我是如何被诽谤的，我不会罢休的，因为我并无恶意。

sentences.en: I can do what I like.
sentences.zh: 我想做什么就做什么。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Just a friendly kiss.
sentences.zh: 只是一个友好的吻。

sentences.en: Just a bit of fun.
sentences.zh: 只是闹着玩儿罢了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: People may wonder what about Catherine.
sentences.zh: 人们可能会想，凯瑟琳呢？

sentences.en: You know, is she becoming suspicious?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，她开始起疑心了吗？

sentences.en: I think she is to a degree, but he does not rein in his behaviour at all.
sentences.zh: 我想她在某种程度上是怀疑的，但他一点也没有收敛自己的行为。

sentences.en: And actually it all gets a bit weird with Thomas Eymour and Catherine and Elizabeth.
sentences.zh: 事实上，托马斯·西摩、凯瑟琳和伊丽莎白之间的关系变得有点诡异。

sentences.en: So there's one very bizarre occasion when Catherine and Elizabeth are out walking in the garden and Thomas surprises them and he cuts Elizabeth's gown and I quote,
sentences.zh: 所以有一个非常离奇的场合，凯瑟琳和伊丽莎白在花园里散步，托马斯突然出现，他把伊丽莎白的裙子剪破了，我引用原话，

sentences.en: in a hundred pieces, what's kind of more bizarre still is that according to Elizabeth, the Queen held her while the Lord Admiral cut it.
sentences.zh: 剪成了一百多片，更离奇的是，据伊丽莎白所说，王后在一旁按住她，任由海军大臣把裙子剪了。

sentences.en: So it's quite odd, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以这真的很古怪，不是吗？

sentences.en: That is pretty weird.
sentences.zh: 这挺诡异的。

sentences.en: What's Catherine Parr thinking during all this?
sentences.zh: 凯瑟琳·帕尔在这一切发生时是怎么想的？

sentences.en: One theory is that maybe it was a bet, a bit of fun.
sentences.zh: 有一种理论认为，这也许只是个赌局，一种好玩的小游戏。

sentences.en: I think Catherine wants to believe that, that it's just innocent fun.
sentences.zh: 我觉得凯瑟琳愿意相信那是无伤大雅的玩笑。

sentences.en: But I think that in the build up to, you know, the Christmas break, I think she's clearly hoping that if Elizabeth goes away, maybe when she comes back,
sentences.zh: 但我觉得，你知道的，在圣诞假期临近的这段时间里，她显然希望如果伊丽莎白离开，等她回来时，

sentences.en: everything will be sorted out and Thomas Eymour will be keeping his hands in his pockets.
sentences.zh: 一切都会解决，托马斯·西摩也会安分守己。

sentences.en: The problem is that's not what happens.
sentences.zh: 问题是，事情并没有那样发展。

sentences.en: So the moment Elizabeth is back, Seymour is up to his old tricks, coming to her bedroom each morning in his nightgown, bare legged in his slippers.
sentences.zh: 所以伊丽莎白刚一回来，西摩就故态复萌，每天早上穿着睡袍、光着腿、趿着拖鞋来到她的卧室。

sentences.en: And Elizabeth, by now, has developed a strategy, which is that if he bursts in on her, she reaches for a book and puts her nose in the book.
sentences.zh: 而此时的伊丽莎白已经想好了一套对策，那就是每当他突然闯进来，她就拿过一本书，把头埋进去看书。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Hoping that the sight of some Greek verses or something will keep him at bay.
sentences.zh: 希望能用几行希腊文或其他什么东西让他知难而退。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，正是如此。

sentences.en: Cat, she upbraids Seymour again.
sentences.zh: 凯特又一次严厉斥责了西摩。

sentences.en: Again, it has no effect.
sentences.zh: 然而，依然毫无作用。

sentences.en: And then that spring, the crisis point, which was kind of always going to arrive, does finally arrive because Catherine, and again to quote,
sentences.zh: 然后在那个春天，那种似乎总会来临的危机时刻终于到来了，因为凯瑟琳——借用原文来说——

sentences.en: came suddenly upon them where they were all alone, he having her in his arMs.
sentences.zh: 突然撞见他们独处，他把她抱在怀里。

sentences.en: He having her in his arms is ambiguous though, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 不过“他把她抱在怀里”这句话很含糊，不是吗？

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Because they're alone together, you know, in an embrace.
sentences.zh: 因为他们俩当时独处，你知道的，正搂抱在一起。

sentences.en: Is that voluntary or is that involuntary?
sentences.zh: 那是自愿的还是非自愿的？

sentences.en: It's not clear.
sentences.zh: 这并不清楚。

sentences.en: It's unclear.
sentences.zh: 说不清楚。

sentences.en: And I think it's unclear to Catherine.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得对凯瑟琳来说也是一头雾水。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And she is very heavily pregnant by this point and obviously incredibly upset.
sentences.zh: 此时她的孕相已经非常明显，显然难过极了。

sentences.en: And I think that perhaps she fears the worst, that Elizabeth has been complicit in this.
sentences.zh: 我想她可能做最坏的打算，担心伊丽莎白是这事的同谋。

sentences.en: And so she sends Elizabeth away.
sentences.zh: 于是她把伊丽莎白打发走了。

sentences.en: Elizabeth goes to a place called Chessent in Hertfordshire.
sentences.zh: 伊丽莎白去了赫特福德郡一个叫切森特的地方。

sentences.en: And there she stays with Kate Astley's sister and her husband, who's a guy called Sir Anthony Denny.
sentences.zh: 她在那里和凯特·阿斯利的姐姐以及她的丈夫住在一起，那人叫安东尼·丹尼爵士。

sentences.en: And the salient thing about Sir Anthony Denny, the one thing that everybody knows about him and why his service has been so valued by Henry VIII,
sentences.zh: 关于安东尼·丹尼爵士最重要的一点——也就是人人都知道的关于他的一点，以及为什么亨利八世如此看重他的服务——

sentences.en: is that he's a courtier chiefly celebrated for his ability to keep a secret.
sentences.zh: 在于他是一位主要以守口如瓶而闻名的朝臣。

sentences.en: And obviously both Elizabeth and Catherine are paranoid that gossip may leak, that the story may break.
sentences.zh: 显而易见，伊丽莎白和凯瑟琳都患上了被迫害妄想症，担心闲言碎语会泄露，内幕会曝光。

sentences.en: All that summer they're kind of waiting really for the rumours to spread.
sentences.zh: 整个夏天，她们基本上都在提心吊胆地等着谣言四处散播。

sentences.en: And actually they seem not to.
sentences.zh: 然而事实上，谣言似乎并没有传开。

sentences.en: And that's a source of great relief to both of them.
sentences.zh: 这让她们俩都大大松了一口气。

sentences.en: And Elizabeth and Catherine are writing regularly to each other.
sentences.zh: 伊丽莎白和凯瑟琳经常互通书信。

sentences.en: They obviously want to repair their relationship.
sentences.zh: 她们显然想要修复彼此的关系。

sentences.en: And Catherine writes to Elizabeth and says, you know, if I hear anything bad, any story slipping out, I will write immediately and let you know.
sentences.zh: 凯瑟琳写信给伊丽莎白说，你知道的，如果我听到任何坏消息，有什么风声走漏，我会立刻写信通知你。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So clearly by this point they are back on side.
sentences.zh: 所以很显然，到这个时候她们已经重修旧好了。

sentences.en: Their relationship has been patched up.
sentences.zh: 她们的关系已经破镜重圆。

sentences.en: But then there's a twist, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 但随后又出现了转折，对吧？

sentences.en: There is a twiSt. Yeah.
sentences.zh: 确实有转折。是的。

sentences.en: I mean, you described Catherine of being pregnant.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你之前形容凯瑟琳怀孕了。

sentences.en: She goes off to one of the Seymour estates that summer.
sentences.zh: 那个夏天她去了西摩家族的一处庄园。

sentences.en: Soodley Castle.
sentences.zh: 苏德利城堡。

sentences.en: Very nice castle, I have to say.
sentences.zh: 我得说，那是一座非常不错的城堡。

sentences.en: And I have to say, I commend it because when I was a boy, they had, to my mind, a world leading adventure playground.
sentences.zh: 而且我必须说，我高度赞赏它，因为我小时候，在我看来，那里有一个世界领先的冒险游乐场。

sentences.en: So that's nice.
sentences.zh: 所以那挺不错的。

sentences.en: Oh.
sentences.zh: 噢。

sentences.en: Anyway, she goes to Soodley Castle.
sentences.zh: 言归正传，她去了苏德利城堡。

sentences.en: She gives birth to a girl called Mary, doesn't she, on the 30th of August?
sentences.zh: 她在8月30日生下了一个叫玛丽的女孩，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, who's named after Mary Tudor, interestingly.
sentences.zh: 是的，有趣的是，这个孩子是按玛丽·都铎的名字命名的。

sentences.en: Oh, that's nice.
sentences.zh: 噢，那挺好的。

sentences.en: And then she drops dead.
sentences.zh: 然后她就突然暴毙了。

sentences.en: Very sad.
sentences.zh: 真令人痛心。

sentences.en: So that's the end of Catherine Parr.
sentences.zh: 凯瑟琳·帕尔的故事就这样结束了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So it's very Jane Seymour.
sentences.zh: 这太像简·西摩的命运了。

sentences.en: She dies of a postnatal fever and she's buried two days later in the church at Soodley Castle.
sentences.zh: 她死于产褥热，两天后被安葬在苏德利城堡的教堂里。

sentences.en: And it's notable, I learnt, for two firsts.
sentences.zh: 我了解到，这场葬礼有两个创纪录的特别之处。

sentences.en: So the first of these is that, I learnt this from Nicola Tallis' book on the young Elizabeth.
sentences.zh: 其中第一个是——我是从尼古拉·塔利斯关于年轻伊丽莎白的书中了解到的——

sentences.en: Catherine Parr is the only English queen to be buried on a private estate.
sentences.zh: 凯瑟琳·帕尔是唯一一位被安葬在私人领地的英国王后。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And I learnt from David Starkey that her funeral was the first Protestant royal funeral.
sentences.zh: 而我从大卫·斯塔基那里得知，她的葬礼是第一场新教皇室葬礼。

sentences.en: And that very, very devoutly Protestant ward of Sir Thomas Seymour, Lady Jane Grey, plays the role of Chief Mourner.
sentences.zh: 作为托马斯·西摩爵士那位极其虔诚的新教庇护对象，简·格雷女士在其中扮演了首席送葬者的角色。

sentences.en: Oh, that's interesting.
sentences.zh: 噢，这很有意思。

sentences.en: But for Elizabeth, this is another crushing blow.
sentences.zh: 但对伊丽莎白来说，这又是沉重的一击。

sentences.en: I mean, for somebody born into, you know, what you might say, immense privilege and wealth, she's had a really bad run, hasn't she?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，对于一个生来就拥有你可能会说的那种巨大特权和财富的人来说，她的人生遭遇真的太惨了，不是吗？

sentences.en: Basically, everybody that she's got close to has died.
sentences.zh: 基本上，她所有亲近过的人都去世了。

sentences.en: Educationalists, mother, father.
sentences.zh: 家庭教师、母亲、父亲。

sentences.en: And lost two stepmothers to childbirth.
sentences.zh: 并且有两位继母死于生育。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And again, you have to wonder what impact does this have on her long-term attitude to the prospects of motherhood?
sentences.zh: 而且你不得不思考，这会对她未来对待为人母的前景产生什么长期影响？

sentences.en: Yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 对，当然会。

sentences.en: Not to over-psychologise it again.
sentences.zh: 虽然这话听起来可能又有点过度心理分析了。

sentences.en: Although one thing that does occur to me, think about Elizabeth's prospects.
sentences.zh: 不过有一件事确实让我浮想联翩，那就是想想伊丽莎白的前景。

sentences.en: So, Thomas Seymour, he's very dashing, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 所以，托马斯·西摩，他非常有魅力，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, I know he's something of a mystical, but he's very dashing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我知道他有点神秘兮兮的，但他确实很有魅力。

sentences.en: He's now a widower and he would be a bit of a catch, would he not?
sentences.zh: 他现在是个鳏夫，而且算得上是一个不错的结婚对象，不是吗？

sentences.en: And Elizabeth is 15 years old and would be a catch in her own right.
sentences.zh: 而伊丽莎白当时15岁，本身也是一个极具吸引力的成婚人选。

sentences.en: So, is there some possibility that he might?
sentences.zh: 所以，他有没有可能会动心呢？

sentences.en: Well, Thomas Seymour, I think, seems genuinely upset at the loss of his wife.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我觉得托马斯·西摩在失去妻子这件事上，似乎是真心感到难过。

sentences.en: I think he genuinely loved Catherine and was distraught when she died.
sentences.zh: 我认为他是真心爱着凯瑟琳的，并在她去世时悲痛欲绝。

sentences.en: But you are right.
sentences.zh: 但你说得对。

sentences.en: The fact that she is now dead does mean that he is back on the market.
sentences.zh: 她现在已经去世这一事实，确实意味着他又回到了单身汉的市场中。

sentences.en: And he must be looking at Elizabeth as a very nubile candidate.
sentences.zh: 而且他肯定把伊丽莎白视为一个非常成熟迷人的候选人。

sentences.en: She is all the more on his mind because by this point, he is massively on manoeuvres, looking to topple his brother, the protector.
sentences.zh: 她在他脑海中挥之不去，因为此时此刻，他正大举密谋，企图推翻他的哥哥——摄政王。

sentences.en: He has been very much playing the fun uncle with Edward VI.
sentences.zh: 他一直在和爱德华六世扮演着好玩有趣的叔叔角色。

sentences.en: So, his elder brother, the Duke of Somerset, is always coming with issues about problems in Scotland or tax or whatever.
sentences.zh: 所以，他的大哥萨默塞特公爵总是带着苏格兰问题、税收或其他种种麻烦找上门来。

sentences.en: Thomas Seymour is turning up with gifts of money and amusingly spiced cakes, all that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 而托马斯·西摩却带着金钱礼物和风味独特的香料蛋糕出现，诸如此类。

sentences.en: What spice would that be that would be so amusing?
sentences.zh: 那到底是什么香料能让人觉得这么有趣呢？

sentences.en: It would be fun.
sentences.zh: 这会很有趣。

sentences.en: That's the point.
sentences.zh: 这就是重点所在。

sentences.en: It's fun.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣。

sentences.en: Some fun cinnamon.
sentences.zh: 一些有趣的肉桂。

sentences.en: Fun cinnamon.
sentences.zh: 有趣的肉桂。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And basically, his plan is to seize control of the king physically.
sentences.zh: 而且基本上，他的计划是以武力控制国王。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And by doing that, to force a change of government.
sentences.zh: 并通过这种方式，迫使政府发生更迭。

sentences.en: And if he can marry Elizabeth, then obviously that would then consolidate his power.
sentences.zh: 如果他能娶到伊丽莎白，那么显然这将巩固他的权力。

sentences.en: He'd be absolutely the power behind the throne.
sentences.zh: 他绝对会成为王位背后的实际掌权者。

sentences.en: Elizabeth, meanwhile, has left Chessent, where she was hanging out with the very discreet husband of Kate.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，伊丽莎白已经离开了切森特，在那里她一直和凯特的那个非常谨慎的丈夫待在一起。

sentences.en: Anthony Denny.
sentences.zh: 安东尼·丹尼。

sentences.en: And she's gone back to Hatfield, her childhood home.
sentences.zh: 她回到了她的童年宅邸哈特菲尔德。

sentences.en: And here, for the first time, she presides over a residence as her own mistress.
sentences.zh: 在这里，她生平第一次作为女主人主理一处宅邸。

sentences.en: You know, she is now her own woman.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，她现在可以自己作主了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And when she's traveling from Chessent to Hatfield, she's accompanied by members of Seymour's household, you know, servants of his.
sentences.zh: 当她从切森特前往哈特菲尔德时，随行的是西摩府邸的成员，也就是他的仆人们。

sentences.en: And one of them speaks to Kate Ashley, who is obviously riding with Elizabeth, and passes on a message for Elizabeth from Thomas Seymour.
sentences.zh: 其中一人与凯特·阿什利交谈——凯特显然是和伊丽莎白同行的——并向伊丽莎白转达了来自托马斯·西摩的信息。

sentences.en: I think it suggests that his conversation with Elizabeth may not have been just about ancient Greek, I suspect.
sentences.zh: 我猜这表明他与伊丽莎白的对话，恐怕不仅仅局限于古希腊语。

sentences.en: Which doesn't reflect terribly well, I think, on Thomas Seymour.
sentences.zh: 我认为这给托马斯·西摩带来的评价实在算不上多好。

sentences.en: And also, I don't think it reflects very well on Kate that she's passed it on.
sentences.zh: 而且，我也觉得凯特把话传了话这一举动，同样很不光彩。

sentences.en: And it has to be said that by this point, she's behaving very inappropriately.
sentences.zh: 必须指出的是，到了这个时候，她的行为已经非常不合时宜了。

sentences.en: Because people remember that she's been confronting Thomas Seymour when he was married to Catherine.
sentences.zh: 因为人们还记得，当托马斯·西摩和凯瑟琳结婚时，她曾与其公开对抗。

sentences.en: But now Catherine's dead.
sentences.zh: 但现在凯瑟琳去世了。

sentences.en: Kate seems to have completely fallen for him.
sentences.zh: 凯特似乎彻底迷上了他。

sentences.en: She seems to have had a bit of a crush on him and has decided that actually he'd be a great husband for Elizabeth.
sentences.zh: 她似乎对产生了一些迷恋，并认定其实他会是伊丽莎白的一个绝佳丈夫。

sentences.en: And so she's kind of endlessly saying to Elizabeth, I really think you should go for him.
sentences.zh: 因此她开始没完没了地对伊丽莎白说，我真的觉得你应该选他。

sentences.en: And meanwhile, Seymour has also been checking with Thomas Parry, the Welshman, for our Welsh listeners, about the state of her finances.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，西摩还向托马斯·帕里——用我们威尔士听众的话说，这位威尔士人——打听伊丽莎白的财务状况。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So he's asking how many persons she kept, what houses she had, what lands.
sentences.zh: 所以他询问她身边养了多少人，拥有哪些宅邸和土地。

sentences.en: And Thomas Parry, I'm afraid to say, like Kate, has been completely seduced by Seymour's charisma.
sentences.zh: 恐怕不得不说，托马斯·帕里和凯特一样，已经被西摩的个人魅力彻底迷住了。

sentences.en: Basically tells him everything.
sentences.zh: 基本上是知无不言。

sentences.en: So essentially, the two people who Elizabeth most trusts, Kate and Parry, are both saying to her, go for it.
sentences.zh: 所以从根本上说，伊丽莎白最信任的两个人，凯特和帕里，都在劝她放手去追。

sentences.en: Thomas Seymour himself is sending lewd messages about her buttocks.
sentences.zh: 托马斯·西摩本人则发一些关于她臀部的下流信息。

sentences.en: And so what is Elizabeth herself making of this?
sentences.zh: 那么伊丽莎白本人对此作何感想呢？

sentences.en: And I think looking at the evidence, there is a sense that she is actually tempted.
sentences.zh: 我认为从种种迹象来看，她其实有些心动。

sentences.en: Because one of the reasons why I think Kate does support Seymour's advances is that she has seen that Elizabeth does fancy Seymour.
sentences.zh: 因为我认为凯特之所以支持西摩的追求，原因之一就是她看出伊丽莎白确实对西摩有好感。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because you said, I mean, it's important to stress, he's very charismatic and good looking, right?
sentences.zh: 因为你曾说过，我的意思是，必须强调的是，他非常有魅力而且长相英俊，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean, he's by all accounts a very, very attractive man.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，据各方所说，他是一个非常非常有吸引力的男人。

sentences.en: And Kate notes how sometimes she would blush when he was spoken of.
sentences.zh: 凯特注意到，有时别人提到他时，她会脸红。

sentences.en: You know, and it's not unknown for victims of sexual abuse to kind of fall for the person who's abusing them.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，性虐待的受害者爱上虐待自己的人，这种事也并非闻所未闻。

sentences.en: Well, or for teenage girls to have a crush on a not much older man, right?
sentences.zh: 好吧，或者说十几岁的女孩对一个只大了一点点的男人产生迷恋，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, it's not unknown.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这并不是什么新鲜事。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So to quote David Starkey on this, it was an initiation and a brutal one into the world of adult sexuality.
sentences.zh: 借用大卫·斯塔基对此的话来说，这是一场成人性爱世界的残酷启蒙。

sentences.en: Almost all the men that she subsequently loved or pretended to love resembled Seymour.
sentences.zh: 她后来几乎所有爱过或假装爱过的男人，都有点像西摩。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有趣。

sentences.en: I mean, it's very interesting, as we will see as we carry the story on.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，正如我们在后续故事中所看到的，这非常有趣。

sentences.en: And because of this, because there was an evident partiality on Elizabeth's part towards Seymour, there was gossip that she had surrendered to his advances.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，由于伊丽莎白对西摩明显偏爱，外界开始有流言蜚语称她已经向他的追求屈服了。

sentences.en: So that when Catherine Parr found Elizabeth in Seymour's arms, the implication was that, you know, Elizabeth had welcomed this.
sentences.zh: 因此，当凯瑟琳·帕尔在西摩怀里发现伊丽莎白时，暗含的意思就是，你知道的，伊丽莎白对此是欣然接受的。

sentences.en: And there are some who say that she'd lost her virginity to him.
sentences.zh: 有些人甚至说她已经把贞洁失给了他。

sentences.en: And there are others who say even that she'd had his child.
sentences.zh: 还有人甚至说她怀上了他的孩子。

sentences.en: There is no substantive evidence for any of this.
sentences.zh: 没有任何实质性证据能够证明这些说法。

sentences.en: And I think that the lack of privacy in Tudor households being what it was, I think it's most improbable.
sentences.zh: 考虑到都铎时期府邸里毫无隐私可言的状况，我认为这极其不可能。

sentences.en: But there's also another, I think, even more salient reason for rejecting these stories.
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，我认为还有一个更明显的理由来驳斥这些传闻。

sentences.en: And that is the evident steeliness, the self-discipline, which Elizabeth displays throughout the affair.
sentences.zh: 那就是伊丽莎白在整起事件中表现出的坚定沉着和自我克制。

sentences.en: It is a maturity that is astonishing, I think, in One So Young.
sentences.zh: 在一个如此年轻的人身上展现出这种成熟，实在是令人惊叹。

sentences.en: Because she, unlike Kate, unlike Parry, actually unlike Thomas Seymour himself, completely understands the impossibility of her marrying him.
sentences.zh: 因为她——不同于凯特、不同于帕里，甚至不同于托马斯·西摩本人——完全明白她嫁给他是根本不可能的事。

sentences.en: And she sums it up completely bluntly.
sentences.zh: 而她对此进行了极其直截了当的总结。

sentences.en: The council will not consent to it.
sentences.zh: 议会将不会同意此事。

sentences.en: But Seymour's plan to marry her, it's not like a kind of private relationship.
sentences.zh: 但西摩想要娶她的计划，并不只是一种私人关系。

sentences.en: It touches directly on the affairs of state.
sentences.zh: 它直接触及了国家事务。

sentences.en: And there is no way that any number of vested interests will allow this marriage to go ahead.
sentences.zh: 任何既得利益集团都不可能允许这桩婚姻继续下去。

sentences.en: And so Elizabeth, knowing this and knowing that Seymour is essentially pushing it, has clearly come to an understanding that he's a very intemperate man.
sentences.zh: 因此，伊丽莎白深知这一点，也清楚西摩基本上是在一意孤行，她显然已经认识到这是一个极其鲁莽冲动的人。

sentences.en: And this represents a threat not just to himself, but if she is caught up in his kind of web to her as well.
sentences.zh: 这不仅对他自己构成了威胁，如果她被卷入他的网中，也会对她构成威胁。

sentences.en: Just a very quick observation, we've mentioned in the last episode that we did a series about Mary Queen of Scots in July, I think it was, this summer.
sentences.zh: 顺便简单提一句，我们在上一集中提到过，今年夏天大约7月份的时候，我们做过一个关于苏格兰女王玛丽的系列节目。

sentences.en: Isn't this the massive contrast between these two characters who are so often opposed to each other?
sentences.zh: 这难道不是这两个性格截然相反、又经常被放在一起对比的人物之间的巨大反差吗？

sentences.en: The Mary Queen of Scots, again and again, in this situation, always goes with her heart.
sentences.zh: 苏格兰女王玛丽在面对这种情况时，一次又一次地总是遵从自己的内心。

sentences.en: She makes poor political choices because she can never step back from her own desires, as it were.
sentences.zh: 她做出了糟糕的政治抉择，因为她仿佛永远无法克制自己的欲望。

sentences.en: And Elizabeth, the thing that marks her out is that she always has that kind of sliver of ice and that very political brain.
sentences.zh: 而伊丽莎白，她的过人之处在于她始终保有一丝理智和极其清醒的政治头脑。

sentences.en: Even when she's, what, 15 years old or whatever she is, she's thinking strategically and she's sensible and she's weighing up the odds and all of this kind of thing,
sentences.zh: 即使是在她十五岁左右或者无论多大的时候，她都在进行战略思考，为人明智，权衡利弊，诸如此类，

sentences.en: which means she doesn't make mistakes.
sentences.zh: 这也意味着她不会犯错。

sentences.en: And also what you see in this business, perhaps for the first time, is a feature of her character that will run and run and run,
sentences.zh: 而且在这场风波中，你也许第一次看到她性格中一个将贯穿始终的特质，

sentences.en: which is that she never commits herself to anything.
sentences.zh: 那就是她从不对任何事做出确切的承诺。

sentences.en: So when Kate presses Seymour's suit, she is non-committal, according to one version, according to another.
sentences.zh: 因此，当凯特为西摩说媒时，根据某种说法，她态度暧昧不明；而根据另一种说法，

sentences.en: Her refusal is absolute.
sentences.zh: 她的拒绝是斩钉截铁的。

sentences.en: But she is very, very good at playing a dead bat, at not being histrionic in her refusals, at being studiedly ambiguous.
sentences.zh: 但她非常擅长打太极，在拒绝时避免表现得戏剧化，并保持一种刻意的模棱两可。

sentences.en: And it's just as well, because early in 1549, it all goes tits up for Thomas Seymour.
sentences.zh: 这实在是明智之举，因为在1549年初，托马斯·西摩的一切彻底搞砸了。

sentences.en: So on the 16th of January, he breaks into the King's private apartments at Whitehall.
sentences.zh: 因此，在1月16日，他闯入了怀特霍尔宫国王的私人寝宫。

sentences.en: And unfortunately for him, there's a dog sleeping outside Edward's door and the dog starts barking at him.
sentences.zh: 但不幸的是，爱德华的门外睡着一只狗，那只狗开始对大声吠叫。

sentences.en: And so Thomas Seymour draws his sword and runs the dog through.
sentences.zh: 于是托马斯·西摩拔出剑，一剑刺穿了那只狗。

sentences.en: He's the Jeremy Thorpe of Tudor politics.
sentences.zh: 他简直就是都铎政治里的杰里·索普。

sentences.en: Yeah, or like Anne of Denmark, James I's wife, who shot his favourite hunting dog.
sentences.zh: 对，或者就像詹姆斯一世的妻子丹麦的安妮那样，她射杀了他最喜欢的猎犬。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: There's quite a lot of dog murder going on.
sentences.zh: 这发生了相当多的虐杀狗事件。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But this is, I think, is the first major example of it.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得这是这方面的第一个重大例子。

sentences.en: And so Thomas Seymour then, oh God, I've killed the King's dog.
sentences.zh: 所以托马斯·西摩当时想，天哪，我把国王的狗给杀了。

sentences.en: This isn't going well.
sentences.zh: 这情况可不妙。

sentences.en: And so he just runs.
sentences.zh: 于是他直接逃跑了。

sentences.en: And then the next day he pretends that nothing's happened and he kind of saunters around and goes to Parliament and all this stuff.
sentences.zh: 而在第二天，他假装什么都没发生过，大摇大摆地四处闲逛，还去参加了议会等等。

sentences.en: But he's been seen.
sentences.zh: 但他已经被看到了。

sentences.en: And so by the evening, he is in the Tower of London.
sentences.zh: 因此到了傍晚，他已经被关进了伦敦塔。

sentences.en: For killing the King's dog or because people think there's some more sinister design behind this?
sentences.zh: 是因为杀死了国王的狗，还是因为人们认为这背后有更险恶的图谋？

sentences.en: Yeah, of course they think it's a more sinister design.
sentences.zh: 对，他们当然觉得这背后有更险恶的图谋。

sentences.en: He's been trying to break into the King's private apartments.
sentences.zh: 他一直在试图闯入国王的私人寝宫。

sentences.en: But for what purpose?
sentences.zh: 但究竟意欲何为？

sentences.en: It doesn't matter.
sentences.zh: 这不重要。

sentences.en: He didn't want to beat him on the buttocks and stuff.
sentences.zh: 他可不是为了去拍打对方的屁股之类的。

sentences.en: It doesn't matter.
sentences.zh: 这不重要。

sentences.en: You are not allowed to break into the King's private apartments.
sentences.zh: 你就是不被允许闯入国王的私人寝宫。

sentences.en: I mean, obviously he's trying to abduct him.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，很显然他是想劫持他。

sentences.en: I think that's the assumption.
sentences.zh: 我想大家都是这么假设的。

sentences.en: And that is treason.
sentences.zh: 而这就是叛国罪。

sentences.en: And that's why he gets sent to the Tower.
sentences.zh: 这就是他被送进伦敦塔的原因。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: And then three days later, Kate Ashley and Thomas Parry are also taken to the Tower.
sentences.zh: 三天后，凯特·阿什利和托马斯·帕里也被带进了伦敦塔。

sentences.en: So now Elizabeth is being drawn into the kind of the vortex of the scandal.
sentences.zh: 于是，伊丽莎白现在也被卷入了这场丑闻的漩涡之中。

sentences.en: Yeah, the whole gang.
sentences.zh: 对，整个团伙都被牵连了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And unsurprisingly, when Elizabeth is informed that her two closest servants have been incarcerated, she was marvelously abashed and did weep very tenderly a long time.
sentences.zh: 毫不意外的是，当伊丽莎白得知她最亲近的两个仆人被关进监狱时，她大受打击，伤心地哭了好久。

sentences.en: And her fears are for her servants, to whom she remains utterly loyal throughout this whole business.
sentences.zh: 她的担忧是为了她的仆人们，在整场风波中，她始终对他们忠心耿耿。

sentences.en: But also, of course, for herself, because she completely understands the mortal peril that she is now in.
sentences.zh: 当然，她也是在为自己担忧，因为她完全明白自己现在正处于致命的危险之中。

sentences.en: And what makes that peril even worse is that Kate and Thomas Parry both end up revealing to their interrogators the full details of Seymour's inappropriate behavior with her.
sentences.zh: 而让这种危险雪上加霜的是，凯特和托马斯·帕里最终都向审讯人员泄露了西摩对她做出不当行为的全部细节。

sentences.en: So all the details that I've been, you know, quoting so far in this episode come from their testimony.
sentences.zh: 所以，我在本集中引用至今的所有细节都来自于他们的供词。

sentences.en: And it's enough to get the interrogators to go and interview Elizabeth.
sentences.zh: 这些已经足够让审讯人员去盘问伊丽莎白了。

sentences.en: And to repeat, she is just a teenage girl at this point.
sentences.zh: 需要重申的是，此时她还只是一个十几岁的女孩。

sentences.en: But she runs rings around her interrogators because she immediately acknowledges the truth of what Kate has revealed.
sentences.zh: 但她把审讯人员耍得团团转，因为她立刻承认了凯特所透露的事情属实。

sentences.en: I mean, she doesn't try to deny it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，她并没有试图否认。

sentences.en: That would have been a very foolish move.
sentences.zh: 那将是一个非常愚蠢的举动。

sentences.en: She's even prepared to acknowledge that she liked Thomas Seymour, that she didn't absolutely detest his advances,
sentences.zh: 她甚至准备承认自己喜欢托马斯·西摩，并不那么讨厌他的追求，

sentences.en: but that she was only prepared to entertain them once the council had first granted its approval.
sentences.zh: 但她只有在议会首先批准的情况下，才愿意考虑这些追求。

sentences.en: And she said enough that there is evidence that supports this claim.
sentences.zh: 而且她的话恰到好处，有证据可以支撑这种说法。

sentences.en: So as a result, it is apparent that she had never been complicit in Seymour's plot.
sentences.zh: 因此，很显然她从未参与西摩的阴谋。

sentences.en: And it's a brilliantly skillful performance from one so young.
sentences.zh: 对于一个如此年轻的人来说，这是一次极其精彩巧妙的应对。

sentences.en: Her interrogators cannot pin anything on her.
sentences.zh: 她的审讯人员抓不到她任何把柄。

sentences.en: They can't show that she was plotting behind Edward's back to marry this man, that she was always operating within the set bounds of legality.
sentences.zh: 他们无法证明她在爱德华背後密谋嫁给这个男人，她一直都在既定的合法范围内行事。

sentences.en: And in due course, Kate and Thomas Parry are released.
sentences.zh: 不久之后，凯特和托马斯·帕里获释了。

sentences.en: And though to begin with, Elizabeth is not allowed to take them back into her service, by September 1549, you know, they're back in her household.
sentences.zh: 尽管一开始，伊丽莎白并未被允许将他们重新招回府邸服务，但到1549年9月，你知道的，他们已经回到了她的府上。

sentences.en: And I think the experience for her was a very salutary one.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这段经历对她来说是非常有益的。

sentences.en: And it confirmed her in an understanding of how politics operates in the nature of men and their desires and their ambitions and the advantages of studied ambiguity
sentences.zh: 这使她更加坚信并理解了政治是如何运作的，了解了人性的本质、他们的欲望与野心，以及刻意保持模糊态度的种种好处，

sentences.en: that will never leave her.
sentences.zh: 这种理解将永远伴随着她。

sentences.en: There will be features of her life, her very long life, right the way up to the end.
sentences.zh: 在她的一生中，在她漫长的一生中，直到最后，都会带有这些特质。

sentences.en: And Thomas Seymour, he ends up on the chopping block, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 而托马斯·西摩，他最终落了个身首异处的下场，不是吗？

sentences.en: He's executed on Tower Hill in the spring of 1549.
sentences.zh: 他在1549年春天于伦敦塔山被处决。

sentences.en: He does.
sentences.zh: 的确如此。

sentences.en: But that ambiguity, doesn't she write to Edward VI and she says to him, it is as your majesty is not unaware, rather characteristic of my nature,
sentences.zh: 但对于这种模棱两可，她不是曾写信给爱德华六世说吗，正如陛下并非不知晓的那样，我的性格中颇具特点的一点，

sentences.en: not to say in words as much as I think in my mind.
sentences.zh: 那就是话语中表达的往往不及我心中所想的。

sentences.en: That's the key, I think.
sentences.zh: 我认为这正是关键所在。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: But that again, I mean, the Mary Queen of Scots parallel,
sentences.zh: 但话说回来，我的意思是，与苏格兰女王玛丽的相似之处在于，

sentences.en: Mary Queen of Scots is unguarded, isn't she?
sentences.zh: 苏格兰女王玛丽毫无防备，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And Elizabeth isn't.
sentences.zh: 而伊丽莎白则不然。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: They are always deep waters with Elizabeth and she's just a brilliant politician.
sentences.zh: 伊丽莎白的心思总是深不可测，她简直是一位出色的政治家。

sentences.en: And a brilliant strategiSt.
sentences.zh: 还是一位杰出的战略家。

sentences.en: So in the wake of Seymour's execution, she's got off, nothing's been pinned on her, but she's aware that she has to tread very carefully now.
sentences.zh: 因此，在西摩被处决之后，她脱身了，没有任何罪名落在他头上，但她意识到自己现在必须如履薄冰。

sentences.en: And so that's what she does.
sentences.zh: 所以她正是这么做的。

sentences.en: She dresses very modestly in black and white.
sentences.zh: 她穿得非常朴素，一身黑白分明。

sentences.en: You know, she's inherited from Anne Boleyn, a love of beautiful clothes.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，她从安妮·博林那里继承了对华丽服饰的热爱。

sentences.en: But for now, she plays the sober Protestant maid.
sentences.zh: 但现在，她扮演着一个稳重的清教徒少女。

sentences.en: And Edward is very impressed.
sentences.zh: 爱德华对此印象深刻。

sentences.en: You know, he's a very priggish Protestant by this point.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，此时的他是一个极其迂腐的清教徒。

sentences.en: And so he calls her sweet sister temperance.
sentences.zh: 因此他亲切地称她为“节制好妹妹”。

sentences.en: He thinks she's great.
sentences.zh: 他认为她棒极了。

sentences.en: She continues her studies under Roger Asham, which she completes in 1550.
sentences.zh: 她在罗杰·阿斯查姆的指导下继续学业，并于1550年完成。

sentences.en: So she's had the best education that anyone in Europe could have, basically.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，她接受了当时全欧洲任何人所能获得的最好教育。

sentences.en: And she is increasingly cast by her admirers as a brilliantly educated woman and by Protestants as a paragon of godly virtue.
sentences.zh: 她的崇拜者越来越将她塑造为一个受过极高教育的女性，而清教徒则将她视为虔诚美德的典范。

sentences.en: So is she a complete paragon?
sentences.zh: 那么，她真的是个完美的典范吗？

sentences.en: I mean, it has to be said that one feature of her character we haven't yet brought out, and that is that she is monumentally acquisitive.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，不得不说，她性格中还有一个我们尚未提及的特点，那就是她有着极强的占有欲。

sentences.en: And again, you can understand that perhaps psychologically.
sentences.zh: 从心理学角度来看，这一点你或许也能理解。

sentences.en: Someone who's led such an unstable life.
sentences.zh: 一个经历过如此动荡生活的人，

sentences.en: She'd want resources that are her own and that she's not dependent upon anyone else to kind of access it.
sentences.zh: 自然会渴望拥有属于自己的资源，并且在获取这些资源时不需要依赖任何人。

sentences.en: But I mean, she does amazingly well.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，她确实做得非常出色。

sentences.en: So by September 1550, which is when she takes legal possession of Hatfield, so this house
sentences.zh: 因此，到1550年9月，也就是她正式合法拥有哈特菲尔德庄园的时候——也就是这座她从小长大的房子，

sentences.en: that she's grown up in, and it legally becomes her property, she's become the second largest landowner in the country.
sentences.zh: 并在法律上正式成为她的财产时，她已经成为了国内第二大地主。

sentences.en: She declared at one stage that she couldn't even remember how many houses she had.
sentences.zh: 她曾在某个阶段宣称，自己甚至记不清究竟拥有多少座宅邸了。

sentences.en: So she's built up, I think, quite a power base for herself.
sentences.zh: 所以我想，她为自己建立了一个相当强大的权力基础。

sentences.en: The kind of the blots on her reputation have been clean.
sentences.zh: 她声誉上的那些污点已经被彻底洗清。

sentences.en: She's admired by the Protestant wing of opinion that is identified with her brother, the king, and she's got financial wherewithal, and land in England is always power.
sentences.zh: 她受到了与她的国王弟弟同气连枝的清教徒派系的赞赏，她拥有雄厚的财力，而在英格兰，土地永远代表着权力。

sentences.en: And this is just as well, because meanwhile, on the public stage, the great game of thrones is continuing.
sentences.zh: 这倒也正合时宜，因为与此同时，在公开的舞台上，伟大的权力游戏仍在继续。

sentences.en: So in January 1552, the Duke of Somerset, the erstwhile lord protector, he's been toppled, and then he follows his brother to the block.
sentences.zh: 因此，在1552年1月，曾任护国公的萨默塞特公爵被推翻了，随后他也步其兄弟的后尘上了断头台。

sentences.en: And a new strongman emerges.
sentences.zh: 一个新的强人崭露头角。

sentences.en: And this is a guy called John Dudley, who is created the Earl of Northumberland.
sentences.zh: 这个人叫约翰·达德利，他被册封为诺森伯兰伯爵。

sentences.en: And this seems good news for Elizabeth.
sentences.zh: 这对伊丽莎白来说似乎是个好消息。

sentences.en: She gets on well with the Dudley family.
sentences.zh: 她与达德利家族关系融洽。

sentences.en: One of Northumberland's sons, Robert Dudley, is a particular playmate of hers, a friend of hers.
sentences.zh: 诺森伯兰的一个儿子罗伯特·达德利，是她特别的玩伴和朋友。

sentences.en: He's a very handsome, dashing, charismatic man.
sentences.zh: 他是一个非常英俊、潇洒且极具魅力的男子。

sentences.en: And it is noted by contemporaries that he has a bit of a resemblance to Thomas Seymour.
sentences.zh: 同时代的人注意到，他身上有几分托马斯·西摩的影子。

sentences.en: So there's something for listeners just to bear in mind.
sentences.zh: 所以这一点值得听众们记在心里。

sentences.en: But all the while, so Elizabeth has basically kind of tied her fortunes to the Protestant wing, to her brother, to Northumberland, to Dudley, to people like that.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，伊丽莎白基本上将自己的命运与清教徒派系、与她的弟弟、与诺森伯兰、与达德利以及诸如此类的人绑定在了一起。

sentences.en: But by the spring of 1553, it's becoming clear to those in the know that this might not have been a good bet, because Edward has fallen mortally ill.
sentences.zh: 然而到了1553年春天，知情人士逐渐清楚地认识到，这可能并不是一笔好买卖，因为爱德华病入膏肓了。

sentences.en: And Edward himself, we've been saying, you know, he's a very vehement Protestant.
sentences.zh: 正如我们之前所说，爱德华本人是个非常激进的清教徒。

sentences.en: He sees it as his duty to ensure a godly successor.
sentences.zh: 他将确保一个虔诚的继承人视为自己的责任。

sentences.en: So a successor who will carry on his work of reformation.
sentences.zh: 也就是一个能将他的宗教改革事业进行到底的继承人。

sentences.en: And the problem for Edward is that, listeners will remember, Henry's final act of succession,
sentences.zh: 对爱德华来说，问题在于，听众们可能还记得，亨利关于王位继承的最终法案

sentences.en: which had been passed in 1543, had prescribed that were Edward to die without having had children, and Edward is still way too young to have had children at this point, then he
